sections.label: New and enhanced enterprise schemes
sections.summary: The Finance Minister introduced new schemes, extended existing ones, and streamlined eight ESG financing schemes into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Besides new schemes, such as Scale‐up SG, Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Co‐Investment Fund III and the Innovation Agent Programme, the Finance Minister has also extended and enhanced existing schemes, such as the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG), the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) and others, with the intent to boost effectiveness and reap better outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Eight existing financing schemes offered by Enterprise Singapore (ESG) were also streamlined into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS), making it simpler for businesses to apply and easier to access the loans.

sections.label: SME Co-Investment Fund III injection
sections.summary: An additional $100 million injection to establish the SME Co-Investment Fund III can act as a catalyst to entice more investments in high-growth potential companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Besides financing, companies that are in the scaling up phase also often need private capital from investors who are more patient and with a longer time horizon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, the additional $100 million injection to establish the SME Co‐Investment Fund III can act as a catalyst to entice even more crucial investments in these high-growth potential companies.

sections.label: Allocation for transforming the economy
sections.summary: Of the $4.6 billion allocated to transforming the economy, $3.6 billion will go towards helping workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Out of the $4.6 billion allocated to transforming the economy, a lion's share of $3.6 billion will go towards helping our workers.

sections.label: PCP jobseeker results
sections.summary: PCP, part of the Adapt and Grow initiative, has helped 76,000 jobseekers find jobs in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: PCP, which is part of the Adapt and Grow initiative, has since achieved encouraging results, helping 76,000 jobseekers find jobs in the last three years.

sections.label: Support for older and low-wage workers
sections.summary: SEC and Additional SEC were extended a year, and WIS payouts of up to $4,000 yearly will help low-wage workers cope with living costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To encourage employment of older workers, the Special Employment Credit (SEC) scheme and the Additional SEC have been extended by another year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SEC provides a wage offset to employers for hiring workers aged above 55 earning up to $4,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The enhancement to the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS) is another piece of welcome news, especially to low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The higher payouts of up to $4,000 per year will help low-wage workers cope with the cost of living.

sections.label: Tightening and S Pass holders
sections.summary: The tightening should signal companies to revamp work processes, redesign jobs and reskill local workers, with almost 200,000 S Pass holders now in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hopefully, this tightening will also signal to companies that they need to revamp their work processes, redesign jobs and reskill their local workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are already almost 200,000 S Pass holders in the workforce now.

sections.label: Reserves investment returns and Budget
sections.summary: Growing Reserves make investment returns the largest revenue contributor, so recent Budgets including 2019 are expansionary, with the NIRC as stimulus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As the base of our Reserves grow, the investment returns have now become the largest revenue contributor, helping us balanced the Budget, which we would otherwise run into deficits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given this is the case, our Budgets in recent years, including Budget 2019, are, by definition, expansionary budgets, with the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) the stimulus injection.

sections.label: Constitution requires balanced Budget
sections.summary: The Constitution requires the Government to maintain a balanced Budget over each term so public funds are allocated sustainably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Constitution requires the Government of the day to maintain a balanced Budget over each term so as to ensure that public funds are allocated sustainably.

sections.label: Utilising accumulated surpluses
sections.summary: With about two years of the term left, the Member asks the Finance Minister how accumulated surpluses for this term will be utilised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With about two more years of the term to go, I would like to ask the Finance Minister how he envisages the accumulated surpluses for this term of government to be utilised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In each of these incidents, the Government has been transparent in getting to the root of the problem, holding the organisations or companies accountable, and each time committing to take the necessary corrective measures.

sections.label: SMEs in Singapore
sections.summary: SMEs make up over 90% of businesses in Singapore and employ 65% of the workforce, so supporting them is key.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) make up more than 90% of the total number of the businesses operating in Singapore and employ 65% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, supporting SMEs to build deep capabilities and grow to stay relevant and competitive are key for both companies and individuals.

sections.label: Enterprise-centric Budget support
sections.summary: The Member welcomes enterprise-centric Budget support, asks about the Innovation Agents Programme criteria, and notes the services sector reduction's message.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I believe that an approach that supports companies at different stages of growth is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the announcement in this year’s Budget to focus support in an enterprise-centric way, noting the different approaches for large companies with complex needs as well as the common challenges that SMEs are facing, and digitalising in common functions like HR, finance and customer relationship management and more targeted support for SMEs as they restructure and grow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat spoke of the introduction of the Innovation Agents Programme where businesses can obtain advice from experienced industry professionals who have both technology expertise and business experience to support their innovation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What are the qualifying criteria for support and how can businesses tap on this programme?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This announcement on the reduction for the services sector had sent a very strong message to companies on the need to be more productive and to rely less on foreign workers.

sections.label: Chatbot solution for drink orders
sections.summary: A chatbot solution from DBS and Every Botty let customers order drinks via Facebook Messenger, raising sales and satisfaction without more workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What they did was that they tested a solution offered by Foodster, a chatbot solution developed by the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) and Every Botty, a chatbot developer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And it allowed them to be able to let their customers chat via Facebook Messenger and order the drinks they want and pick it up and get notification when the drink is ready to go and pick it up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What it meant is that the business was able to achieve greater sales, better customer satisfaction because they picked up the coffee and did not have to wait in the long queue and they did not need to have more workers.

sections.label: Means-testing property annual value
sections.summary: MP asks if the annual value criterion for means-tested schemes can be refined, as the blanket rule may miss its intent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With people living longer and cost of living concerns in a developed market like Singapore, while I agree that these schemes must continue to be means-tested and targeted to provide support for those who most need it, will the Minister give consideration to refining how we use the criterion of annual value of the property lived in?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The current blanket rule of annual value of the property in relation to all who live within the same dwelling unit may miss its intent for scenarios that I had highlighted.

sections.label: Tax collection cost assessment
sections.summary: MP asks whether an assessment was done on how much collecting the tax will cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If this is the case, has assessment been done on how much it is going to cost to collect the tax?

sections.label: Tax collection net revenue
sections.summary: MP asks if collection costs cause net revenue loss, requests anticipated tax amount, and notes travellers must declare expenditure or face fines and prison.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Will the cost of collecting the tax result in net revenue loss from the taxes collected?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the anticipated amount of tax to be collected and the significance to the tax revenue?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Regardless, all Singaporeans traveling will have to be more diligent in declaring their expenditure as failure to declare or incorrectly declaring the expenses does carry fines as well as prison sentences.

sections.label: MGP and Bicentennial Bonus
sections.summary: The $6.1 billion MGP helps half a million Singaporeans born in the 1950s, and the $1.1 billion Bicentennial Bonus helps living expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The MGP of $6.1 billion will provide half a million Singaporeans born in the 1950s better peace of mind in regard to their healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Bicentennial Bonus of $1.1 billion will provide additional help for broad groups of Singaporeans with their living expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This year's Bicentennial Bonus follows last year's $700 million SG Bonus.

sections.label: Venture capital and research funding
sections.summary: Venture capital deals and 150 global funds, incubators and accelerators rose, and $19 billion is set aside for the RIE 2020 Plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We saw a significant rise in venture capital deals and the setting up of 150 global venture capital funds, incubators and accelerators based right here to support startups in Singapore and in the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We invest substantially in scientific research, with $19 billion set aside for the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2020 Plan.

sections.label: ITMs and economic restructuring
sections.summary: ITMs cover 80% of the economy and their progress is central to economic restructuring, innovation, productivity and worker skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With ITMs covering 80% of our economy, their progress is central to our economic restructuring effort to foster innovation, boost productivity and develop skills of workers in their respective industries.

sections.label: WIS income cap adjustment
sections.summary: The WIS qualifying income cap rises from $2,000 to $2,300 per month, providing $1 billion a year to 440,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Many lower-wage workers who previously earned just over $2,000 are rejoicing to see the WIS qualifying income cap being adjusted from $2,000 to $2,300 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: WIS is a key pillar of our social security system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This enhancement will provide $1 billion a year to supplement the income of 440,000 Singaporeans.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus and Special Transfers
sections.summary: The Government's healthy surplus let the Minister for Finance set aside $15.3 billion in Special Transfers, plus $9 billion FY2018 transfers and about $18 billion accumulated surplus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The healthy fiscal surplus accumulated by this Government in its current term has provided significant room for the Minister for Finance to plan ahead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: He set aside a large sum of $15.3 billion under Special Transfers, including $6.1 billion for the MG Fund and $5.08 billion for the Long-Term Care Support Fund, to meet Singaporeans’ long-term needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is on top of the FY2018 Special Transfers of $9 billion for future rail infrastructure and GST Voucher needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the accumulated surplus of about $18 billion from previous years, there is also an ample buffer for counter-cyclical measures should the global economy pose greater downside risks than anticipated.

sections.label: Universal senior citizen healthcare package
sections.summary: The Government should introduce a basic level of medical benefits through a universal and permanent senior citizen healthcare package from age 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address such feedback, the Government should introduce a basic level of medical benefits through a universal and permanent senior citizen healthcare package from the age of 60.

sections.label: NIRC increase and accumulated surpluses
sections.summary: The 35%-odd increase in the NIRC from 2016 partly explains the healthy accumulated surpluses accrued to this term of Government since 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the greater spending needs of the Government that certain Ministers have raised in the past, going forward, the 35%-odd increase in the NIRC from 2016 goes some way to explain the healthy accumulated surpluses accrued to this term of Government from the Opening of Parliament in 2016.

sections.label: Primary healthcare out-of-pocket expenses
sections.summary: The scheme's centrepiece should alleviate out-of-pocket expenses for primary healthcare, addressing cost of living for all Singaporeans from age 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To begin with, the centrepiece of such a scheme should be aimed at alleviating the out-of-pocket expenses for primary healthcare, so as to address cost of living for all Singaporeans from the age of 60.

sections.label: Permanent universal senior medical package
sections.summary: A permanent universal senior citizen medical package would symbolise integration among red passport holders, and its eligibility age should be dispensed with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A permanent and universal senior citizen medical package would also represent a critical symbol of integration among all Singaporeans who hold the red passport, and it would follow that the eligibility age into such permanent schemes should be dispensed with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is particularly so as about 20,000 new citizens are added to the pool of Singaporeans on a yearly basis.

sections.label: Differentiated fiscal strategy intention
sections.summary: The Minister confirmed the Government's intention to pursue a differentiated fiscal strategy for infrastructure investment and recurrent social and security spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During the course of his speech, the Minister confirmed the Government's intention to pursue a differentiated fiscal strategy – one for major infrastructure investment and another for recurrent social and security spending.

sections.label: Borrowing for infrastructure plans
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether market borrowing for infrastructure is limited to Changi's expansion or extends to other long-term infrastructure plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In comparison, at last year’s Budget, four separate infrastructure prongs were highlighted, and these included the expansion of our MRT lines, regional redevelopment including the Jurong Lake District, Punggol Digital District and Woodlands North Coast, the rejuvenation of our Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats and associated infrastructure and finally, Changi Airport Terminal 5 (T5), the Tuas Megaport and the now postponed High-Speed Rail (HSR).

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister clarify if borrowing from the market for infrastructure development is only limited to Changi's expansion or does it extend to the other long-term infrastructure plans shared by the Minister last year?

sections.label: Estimates for infrastructure spending
sections.summary: The Minister said preliminary estimates had been carried out, and the speaker asks for the estimates, financing approach and required infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister shared that while it was difficult to project such spending, some preliminary estimates had been carried out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide a sense of these estimates, the financing approach and the infrastructure required for this purpose?

sections.label: Greening and urban heat island
sections.summary: Researchers posited that greening by itself contributes little to mitigate the urban heat island effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Researchers posited that greening, it and of itself, contributes little to mitigate the urban heat island effect.

sections.label: Freedom of information laws
sections.summary: About 80 of the 110 or so countries with freedom of information laws introduced such legislation in the last 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since the days of decolonisation, numerous countries have introduced some form of legalisation that promotes greater transparency and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, out of the 110 or so countries in the world today which host some form of a freedom of information law, about 80 introduced such legislation only in the last 30 years or so.

sections.label: Singaporeans crunching Budget numbers
sections.summary: Some well-meaning Singaporeans want to crunch Budget numbers themselves and understand policy tradeoffs but are not necessarily able to do so today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, insofar as the Budget is concerned, enough well-meaning Singaporeans do not just want to take the Government at its word but want to crunch the numbers themselves and better understand policy tradeoffs, but they are not necessarily able to do so today.

sections.label: Reserves financing Budget
sections.summary: About 20% of the Budget is financed by proceeds from the Reserves, making the issue relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With about 20% of our Budget financed by proceeds from our Reserves, one can understand why this issue is a relevant one.

sections.label: Confident population as X factor
sections.summary: A confident population, not an insecure one, will determine how united and strong tomorrow's Singapore is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The need for a confident population, as opposed to an insecure one, will be the "X" factor that determines how united and strong the Singapore of tomorrow will be.

sections.label: DRC reduction to 35%
sections.summary: Budget 2019 continues the latest DRC reduction to 35% in 2021, likely hitting hospitality, F&B, arts, entertainment and lifestyle sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As Budget 2019 continues with the latest DRC reduction to 35% in 2021, sectors likely to be hit will be in hospitality, F&B services, the arts, entertainment and other lifestyle sectors.

sections.label: Pan Pacific employing disabled persons
sections.summary: Mr Andreas Sugaimin of Pan Pacific Hotel group has embarked on a programme to employ persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Mr Andreas Sugaimin, Senior Vice President of Human Capital and Development of Pan Pacific Hotel group, in his efforts to employ local staff, has embarked on a programme to employ persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Tiered support for SMEs
sections.summary: Budget 2019 adopts a tiered approach giving different help to SMEs of different sizes, with high-growth large firms getting more support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Instead of broad strokes, a different tiered approach is explicitly adopted in Budget 2019 to provide different strokes of help to SMEs of different sizes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, high-growth large firms get more dedicated support and account management to scale and internationalise, such as using the Scale-Up SG programme.

sections.label: Five measures for local employment
sections.summary: Five measures are listed, including developing a special workforce, incentivising SMEs, and updating source countries, though many SMEs remain unaware.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, aggressively identify, train and develop a special workforce comprising senior citizens and persons with disabilities; two, incentivise SMEs through higher SEC to employ these special workforce members; three, provide a buffer foreign headcount for a duration if an employer guarantees the training and employment of, say, more than 10 local staff with disadvantaged backgrounds; four, update the pool of source countries to include countries, such as Myanmar, to allow employers to fulfil the DRC; and five, adopt and execute well a four-pronged process to nurture the largest base of small and micro SMEs, the largest base of most SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many SMEs are still not fully aware of the purpose and slew of measures the Government has in store for them.

sections.label: VWO financial independence suggestions
sections.summary: The speaker proposes three ways to help VWOs become more financially independent from Government grants and donations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, therefore, I have three suggestions to enhance the financial independence of the VWOs so that they can provide more sustainable quality services with the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I propose that the Government: (a) further incentivise donors to Institutions of a Public Character by offering a 300% tax deduction provision for the Bicentennial Community Fund, similar to that implemented for SG50; (b) help VWOs further earn their own stream of incomes by allowing VWOs to invest in Singapore Savings Bonds, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is currently not permitted; and (c) invest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For Government to invest in and nurture VWOs with good track records and help them build social enterprises and other revenue-earning arms to reduce their dependence on Government grants and donations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Create platforms similar to the enterprise model that we see in the economy side, such as VWOs Go Digital!, Scale Up VWOs!, VWO Co-Investment Fund or even VWOs Go Regional!

sections.label: VWOs regional businesses and independence
sections.summary: The speaker says VWOs could start regional businesses and must be strengthened to be financially independent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is no reason why VWOs cannot start regional businesses offering much-needed training in social services, consulting services and disability management, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And since there is no way that the Government will be able to fund all the needs, it must find ways, like it does for the SMEs, to strengthen its VWO partners so that they, too, can be more financially independent and continue to be a strong service partner to the Government.

sections.label: SMEs backbone of Singapore economy
sections.summary: SMEs form a significant number of enterprises, employ 65% of the workforce and contribute almost 50% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: SMEs continue to be the backbone of Singapore's economy, forming a significant number of all enterprises in Singapore, employing 65% of our workforce and contributing almost 50% of our GDP.

sections.label: SME funding and digital schemes
sections.summary: Schemes like SME Co-Investing Fund III and Enterprise Financing System improve SME funding access, and SMEs are urged to tap digital programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Schemes like the SME Co-Investing Fund III and the Enterprise Financing System are aimed at giving our SMEs a leg-up by improving their access to public and private funding so that they have the much-needed liquidity to import the latest technology, grow their businesses, and possibly eventually spread their wings beyond Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would strongly urge our SMEs to continue to tap on schemes like the Go Digital programme and Digital Services Hub to scale up on their digital solution capabilities and shore up their competencies in the area of the Internet of Things as well.

sections.label: Digital Defence against cyber threats
sections.summary: The speaker cites cyber terrorist risks to key services and welcomes Digital Defence as a sixth total defence pillar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Consider examples of how cyber terrorists could wreak havoc and create massive damage if they gained access and control of key services, such as our emergency services, airports and transportation networks or key installations like power grids.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I am heartened that the Government has introduced a sixth pillar of total defence – Digital Defence – to combat this cyber threat.

sections.label: ComCare long-term assistance scheme
sections.summary: The speaker notes ComCare's shortcomings in repeated extension applications and looks forward to the ComCare Long-Term Assistance scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The current ComCare scheme, for example, is useful in the way that it is meant to provide short-term support, but it does have its shortcomings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the ComCare short-to-medium term assistance that was rendered to them could be extended when needed, the process of putting in the repeated applications for extensions could be discouraging and demoralising for these residents who are already assailed by multiple challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I am looking forward to the ComCare Long-Term Assistance scheme that will help provide a longer-term guarantee to help those who need more support, especially those who are unable to work due to unfavourable conditions and circumstances.

sections.label: Retirement from PSA
sections.summary: In 2018, he retired from PSA after more than 45 years with the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2018, he retired from PSA after more than 45 years with the company.

sections.label: MGP review and top-ups
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to review the MGP and top up benefits so MG have peace of mind in their silver years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are many men and women like Mr Sree who have shown the grit and resolve to not only contribute to the defence, economic growth and societal development of a newly-independent Singapore, but managed to upskill and upgrade themselves along the way, while also somehow finding time to raise a family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These remarkable men and women are responsible for the trees that provide the shade that we are all now enjoying and I would urge the Government to review the MGP from time to time, and to top-up the benefits whenever we are able to so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that this would give the MG peace of mind that their needs would be attended to and they would be looked after during their silver years.

sections.label: Local workforce plateau
sections.summary: The local workforce will plateau from around 2020, with incoming local workers just enough to replace retiring workers and zero net growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For a few years now, we have been reminded that the local workforce in Singapore will plateau from around 2020, which is just next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In other words, based on current employment and retirement rates, the incoming local workers will just be about enough to offset and replace the retiring workers, and there will be zero net growth in the local workforce.

sections.label: Foreigners in workforce
sections.summary: About one in three persons in Singapore's workforce is a foreigner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: About one in three persons in Singapore’s workforce is a foreigner.

sections.label: Fourth tap and older workers
sections.summary: The fourth tap is making the best use of the local working-age population, and MOM has convened a Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, we have to look very carefully at the fourth tap, and the fourth tap is: how do we make the best use of our local population in the working ages, both those currently working, as well as the latent pool waiting to be activated for work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I am grateful that the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has convened a Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers to review retirement and re-employment ages and to consider adjustments to the CPF contribution rates for older workers.

sections.label: Non-working female residents
sections.summary: Close to 170,000 female residents aged 40 to 59 were not working, with about 33,000 citing caregiving as the main reason.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Labour Force Survey 2018, there are close to 170,000 female residents aged between 40 and 59 in Singapore who were not working.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Of these, around one in five, or about 33,000, of them cited caregiving to family members or relatives, excluding childcare, as the main reason for their not being at work.

sections.label: Stay-at-home women want flexible work
sections.summary: A 2017 NTUC survey of 529 stay-at-home women aged 25 to 54 found two in three keen to return to work if suitable part-time or flexible arrangements existed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: A 2017 survey by the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) U Family Secretariat of 529 stay-at-home women aged between 25 and 54 found that two in three of them were keen on returning to the workforce, if only suitable part-time or flexible work arrangements (FWAs) could be found to allow them to balance between earning an income and undertaking caregiving.

sections.label: Singapore mature worker employment rankings
sections.summary: Comparing with OECD countries, Singapore ranks about 10th in full-time employment rates for ages 55 to 64, but 23rd in part-time comparisons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Comparisons of full-time employment rates for mature workers of ages between 55 and 64, comparing Singapore with the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries, it places us at about the 10th position with respect to our full-time employment rates for this group of 55 to 64.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: But when we look at the part-time comparisons, then we go down to the 23rd place, comparing with the OECD countries.

sections.label: Flexible work offered broadly by few
sections.summary: A paragraph states that although 93% of Singapore organisations offer flexible work, only 21% offer it broadly across the organisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In there, there is a paragraph that says, "A closer look at the data shows that although 93% of Singapore organisations offer flexible work, in only 21% is it offered broadly across the organisation.

sections.label: Placement and training for part-time work
sections.summary: Over 40% of jobseekers above 40 helped by e2i are placed mostly full-time, so sectors, training and placement mechanisms for part-time work must be examined.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Today, more than 40% of jobseekers above age 40, as helped by e2i, are successfully placed mostly into full-time jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must identify sectors and occupations with good relative prospects to achieve strong placement outcomes for flexi, part-time work as well.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We must also see whether training and placement mechanisms for part-time work may be different from those for full-time work and, therefore, what may need redesigning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Thirdly, to determine how training and retraining and job matching methods should be adapted to achieve significant improvement in the placement rates into part-time jobs for the targeted returning stream of mature working age Singaporeans, many of whom currently have to make the stark choice between working and caregiving.

sections.label: NTUC welcomes WIS enhancements
sections.summary: NTUC applauds Government efforts for low-wage workers and welcomes WIS enhancements, suggesting a higher cash-to-CPF ratio without impacting the allocated budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: NTUC applauds the Government for its continuous efforts to help low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We welcome the enhancements to the WIS scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Government may want to consider increasing the cash-to-CPF ratio to put more cash in the hands of the low-wage workers to help them better meet their immediate needs, without impacting the allocated budget.

sections.label: Support for Progressive Wage Model
sections.summary: Government and employers have been supportive of the Progressive Wage Model, translating to real outcomes for cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our Government and employers have been very supportive of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM), and this has translated to real outcomes for our cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sections.label: NTUC welcomes EDG worker outcomes
sections.summary: NTUC welcomes the Budget condition that positive outcomes for workers be a core criterion for companies to tap the EDG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this year’s Budget, NTUC welcomes the condition to have positive outcomes for workers as a core criterion for companies to tap on the EDG.

sections.label: Contracts should specify service outcomes
sections.summary: Contracts should specify service outcomes instead of headcounts and be evaluated by price-quality method with higher quality weightage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, contracts should specify service outcomes instead of headcounts and be evaluated more holistically based on the price-quality method, where quality has a higher weightage over price.

sections.label: Avoid price undercutting, adopt tripartite standards
sections.summary: Service providers should not gamble on workers' wages; Government should exclude price undercutting providers and do business only with tripartite standards adopters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Service providers should not gamble on their workers’ wages and welfare and hope that the contract they won through price undercutting will bring them profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I urge the Government Ministries and service buyers to keep a lookout for price undercutting and exclude such service providers from getting contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have been active in encouraging companies and service providers to adopt the tripartite guidelines and standards which promote fair and progressive employment practices, which have also helped to make working conditions better for low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We hope that the Government will only do business with companies that have adopted these tripartite standards.

sections.label: Budget WIS, CHAS, training support
sections.summary: The Government increased WIS payouts and provided CHAS and training support; buyers and providers should conduct business honestly and fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Government has increased the payout under the WIS scheme and provided other forms of assistance like CHAS and training support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is important that service buyers and service providers conduct their business honestly and fairly so that low-wage workers can enjoy better salaries and a better working environment.

sections.label: One in 10 workers self-employed
sections.summary: Today, one in 10 workers are self-employed or freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, one in 10 workers are self-employed or freelancers.

sections.label: NICA represents freelancers, offers PML insurance
sections.summary: NICA was registered and became an NTUC affiliate last month to represent freelancers; NTUC and NICA will collaborate with insurers to offer PML insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A case in point is the formation of the National Instructors and Coaches Association (NICA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was registered with the Registrar of Societies and became an affiliate of NTUC just last month to represent the interests of freelancers who teach sports, enrichment and wellness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Because every freelancer matters, NTUC and NICA's first piece of work is to collaborate with insurers to offer Prolonged Medical Leave (PML) insurance to instructors and coaches.

sections.label: Tripartite Standards adoption by companies
sections.summary: MOM recently reported that 500 companies have adopted the Tripartite Standards when contracting with SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOM recently reported that 500 companies have adopted the Tripartite Standards when contracting with SEPs.

sections.label: Diesel duty increase concerns taxi drivers
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance's announcement that diesel duty will be increased has caused much concern among taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance's announcement that diesel duty will be increased has caused much concern among taxi drivers.

sections.label: Taxi diesel cost increase and rental
sections.summary: The average cost increase after the $850 rebate is about $2 to $3 or up to $4 per day for two shift drivers using about 50 litres daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The average cost increase even after the $850 rebate is about $2 to $3 or up to $4 per day because they use about 50 litres of diesel a day if there are two shift drivers of the diesel taxi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In fact, why is it that they can do more?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is because, firstly, they can consider reducing the daily rental of the taxis which, today, ranges from about $110 to $120.

sections.label: Call for taxi licensing criteria changes
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOT and MOF to include positive worker outcomes in taxi licensing criteria, or consider issuing fuel pump licensing rights to unions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, a lot of the conditions seem to be favouring the operator or beyond the control of the drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and MOF to look at taxi licence operators implementing positive outcomes for workers to form part of the licensing criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps, if the operators are not keen on doing more, the Government can consider issuing fuel pump licensing rights to the unions.

sections.label: Government funding for workers
sections.summary: The Labour Movement is heartened that the Government will dedicate $3.6 billion to help workers thrive and adapt to industrial and technological changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, all of us in the Labour Movement are heartened to hear that the Government will be dedicating $3.6 billion towards helping our workers thrive and adapt to industrial and technological changes.

sections.label: SkillsFuture lifelong learning initiative
sections.summary: The Government rolled out SkillsFuture to encourage lifelong learning, with about 465,000 Singaporeans benefiting from SkillsFuture Credit training subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government rolled out the SkillsFuture initiative to encourage a culture of lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This initiative has done well, with about 465,000 Singaporeans benefiting from SkillsFuture Credit training subsidies.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit and education subsidies
sections.summary: The Government can encourage training by letting SkillsFuture Credit offset local polytechnic and university courses, with possible top-ups and subsidies for mature students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government can encourage workers to go for training and build depth in their chosen fields by allowing all local polytechnic and university courses to be automatically offset by the SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given the more expensive nature of such courses, I would urge the Government to consider providing a top-up to the SkillsFuture Credit to encourage Singaporeans to go for these courses that provide them with more depth to support their career goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Better still, I hope the Government can give all adult Singaporeans a second bite of the cherry by providing education subsidies to mature students who wish to pursue a diploma or degree in our local IHLs.

sections.label: UWEEI polytechnic training agreements
sections.summary: UWEEI signed memorandums of understanding with three polytechnics in the west, east and north to provide workers training courses near their workplace or home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The United Workers of Electronics and Electrical Industries (UWEEI) have signed memorandums of understanding with three polytechnics in the west, east and north to provide workers with a wide variety of training courses at locations close to their workplace or their home.

sections.label: Workplace fatalities and injuries in 2018
sections.summary: Workplace fatalities in 2018 reached a record low of 41 cases, but major and minor injuries increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Workplace fatalities in 2018 have reached a record low of 41 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But despite the decrease in fatalities, the number of major and minor injuries have increased.

sections.label: WICA insurance requirements for employees
sections.summary: Under WICA, all employees doing manual work and all employees earning $1,600 or less per month need to be insured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA), all employees doing manual work, as well as all employees earning $1,600 or less per month need to be insured.

sections.label: Workforce diversity and WSH training
sections.summary: Cultural diversity in the workforce makes training local and foreign workers in workplace safety challenging, and training resources vary across 12 approved providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our workforce is diverse and it is this cultural diversity in our workforce that makes it challenging to train our local and foreign workers in workplace safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There are currently 12 approved training providers that conduct WSH WSQ courses for the construction and metal working industries, but the training resources at each of these training providers can vary significantly.

sections.label: Scale-up SG and worker upskilling programmes
sections.summary: The Scale-up SG and pilot Innovation Agents programmes help enterprises build capabilities, while extending SEC and CSP helps workers upskill for emerging jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For enterprises, the Scale-up SG programme and pilot Innovation Agents programme will help firms build deeper capabilities to innovate and grow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For workers, the extension of SEC and CSP will help them upskill so that they can keep ahead of the curve and be ready for emerging jobs.

sections.label: Older Singaporeans in workforce
sections.summary: Older Singaporeans form a significant part of the workforce, which has a quarter aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Older Singaporeans form a significant part of our workforce, which has a quarter aged 55 and above.

sections.label: e2i clients aged 50 and above
sections.summary: In 2018, more than 40% of clients at NTUC's e2i Career Centre were aged 50 and above, about 30% of them PMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In 2018, more than 40% of clients served at NTUC's e2i Career Centre were aged 50 and above, and approximately 30% of this group were professionals, managers and executives (PMEs).

sections.label: Expanding PCPs into growth areas
sections.summary: Programmes helped mature PMEs enter new job roles, and the Government's move to expand PCPs into new growth areas is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These programmes have been successful in helping many mature PMEs enter new and exciting job roles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We, therefore, welcome the Government’s move to expand PCPs into new growth areas, such as blockchain, prefabrication and the development of embedded software, to support mid-career professionals entering these sectors.

sections.label: NTUC Training Council and Exco
sections.summary: The NTUC Training Council and Training Executive Committee were formed last year to coordinate implementation of training efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To address these issues and make industry transformation "real" for our workers, the NTUC Training Council and the Training Executive Committee (Training Exco) were formed last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Training Exco, which I chair, comprises unionists and senior Government officials to coordinate the implementation of training efforts.

sections.label: Reclustering topics to align with ITMs
sections.summary: Over 200 topics and modules will be reclustered to align to the 23 ITMs to help workers navigate courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Over 200 topics and modules will be reclustered to align to the 23 ITMs to help workers in each of the sector navigate through the courses.

sections.label: U Leap SME bosses network
sections.summary: U Leap, with Human Capital Singapore, will launch a community network for SME bosses in March this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To build a healthy ecosystem that supports transformation efforts, U Leap, together with Human Capital Singapore, will launch a community network for SME bosses in March this year.

sections.label: Company Training Committees and ITMs
sections.summary: The Training Exco will use Company Training Committees to help the Labour Movement, employers and Government operationalise ITMs and support skills development and job placement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Training Exco, through the promulgation of Company Training Committees in the companies, will enable the Labour Movement, employers and the Government to work together more closely to operationalise the ITMs and, in particular, support future skills development and job placement strategies under the various ITMs.

sections.label: Private school graduate employment survey
sections.summary: The PEI Graduate Employment Survey found 47.4% of private school fresh graduates secured full-time jobs six months after graduation, down from 60.1%, with lower median pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The latest PEI Graduate Employment Survey found that only 47.4% of private school fresh graduates secured full-time jobs six months after graduation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This was a steep decline from 60.1% for the previous batch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: They also earned less, drawing a median gross monthly salary of S$2,650, compared to graduates from the local Autonomous Universities (AUs) who earned S$3,400.

sections.label: Student unable to secure tuition grant
sections.summary: He cannot secure a tuition grant because he obtained a previous diploma in 2007, and his school fees of $21,000 per year are unpayable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, he is unable to secure a tuition grant because he has already obtained a previous diploma in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: His school fees will amount to $21,000 per year which he cannot pay.

sections.label: Expanding PCP places for workers
sections.summary: More can be done by expanding PCP places to help Singaporean workers, especially younger ones, obtain a second Nitec, diploma or degree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We hope that more can be done for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It entails expanding the number of PCP places by helping our Singaporean workers, especially younger ones, to obtain a second National ITE Certificate (Nitec), a diploma or degree that will help them better adjust to structural economic changes.

sections.label: Training allowances and Common Entry Programmes
sections.summary: Training allowances like those for PCPs can be provided while workers pick up a second qualification, perhaps as a Reskilling Incentive Scheme, and polytechnics are introducing more Common Entry Programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Similar training allowances, such as those for PCPs, can be provided to them while they pick up their second qualification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Perhaps, along the lines of Workfare Incentive Scheme, we can think about it as a Reskilling Incentive Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our polytechnics are also introducing more Common Entry Programmes in Business, and Information and Digital Technologies (IDT) clusters.

sections.label: Duty to create reskilling culture
sections.summary: Creating a culture of reskilling is the duty of unions, employers and the Government, not just the government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Creating a culture of reskilling is not just a government's duty but the duty of unions, employers and the Government.

sections.label: Workers' concerns on Industrial Relations 4.0
sections.summary: A Labour MP says workers have many concerns about Industrial Relations 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As a Labour Member of Parliament, I know that there are a lot of workers' concerns on Industrial Relations 4.0.

sections.label: HR officer proposing GPS driver tracking
sections.summary: An HR officer tried to convince her boss to install GPS tracking to monitor whether drivers are working.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, I hear of how an HR officer tried to convince her boss to install Global Positioning System (GPS) tracking for drivers, so as to monitor whether a driver is working or not.

sections.label: FairPrice staff above 50
sections.summary: More than 50% of FairPrice's workforce is above 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In terms of staff demographics, more than 50% of FairPrice's workforce is above 50 years old.

sections.label: Self-checkouts accepting cash and cards
sections.summary: Usage stagnated until self-checkouts accepted cash as well as credit cards, causing a jump in transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But after a while, the level of usage stagnated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We realised that not everyone had a credit card and then there were also some who, even though they had one, preferred to use cash and so we started to work on the next generation of self-checkouts which also accepted cash in addition to credit cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Not surprisingly, with this new generation of self-checkouts that accepted cash as well as credit cards, we saw another huge jump in customer transactions at these self-checkouts.

sections.label: Investing in humans alongside technology
sections.summary: The speaker says we should invest more in humans, matching each IT course and resource with one in human relations and HR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One thing we can and should do is to invest more in humans, even as we invest in technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For each course in information technology (IT), data analytics and cybersecurity, we need one on psychology, sociology, human relations; for each new resource in the IT department, a similar one in the HR department.

sections.label: National Committee for Ethics in Science and Technology
sections.summary: The speaker argues for a National Committee for Ethics in Science and Technology to give inputs on hard cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Given the complexity and interlinkages, I think there is a case, and I would argue for a National Committee for Ethics in Science and Technology giving inputs on hard cases at the frontiers of new decisions relating to science and technology.

sections.label: Digital Defence sixth pillar
sections.summary: Digital Defence is added as the sixth pillar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Putting Digital Defence as our sixth pillar is another.

sections.label: Investment not lopsided to technology
sections.summary: Investment cannot be lopsided in favour of technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our investment, therefore, cannot be lopsided in favour of technology.

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Retirement age rises from 62 to 65 and re-employment age from 67 to 70, with over 20 unionised companies already leading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One way to do it is to raise the retirement age from 62 to 65, and the re-employment age from 67 to 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, there are already more than 20 unionised companies which are at the forefront of this.

sections.label: Raising re-employment age with SEC
sections.summary: With the SEC extended to end 2020, raising the re-employment age may benefit workers and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the SEC is further extended to end 2020, it is perhaps timely to raise re-employment age so that both workers and employers can benefit.

sections.label: Recognising pro-training companies
sections.summary: The Government is urged to recognise companies that send workers for training and upgrade job processes, giving them easier access to funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In view of digital transformation and the ageing workforce, ensuring that both SMEs and their workers are pro-training is especially important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government to recognise companies which are willing to send workers for training and willing to upgrade and automate job processes, to positively differentiate them by allowing them to easily tap on Government funding versus companies which do not do so.

sections.label: Subsidies for paid time-off upskilling
sections.summary: The Government should give further subsidies, grants or absentee payroll to employers granting paid time-off to upskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the more enlightened employers who grant workers paid time-off to upskill, the Government should provide further subsidies to companies in the form of grants or outright absentee payroll.

sections.label: Economy growth and forecast
sections.summary: The economy expanded 3.2% last year, with 2019 growth forecast between 1.5% and 3.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, our economy expanded 3.2% while growth is forecast to be in the range of 1.5% to 3.5% in 2019.

sections.label: Automation, skills churn, worker outcomes
sections.summary: A study says 44% of work activities can be automated and a third of skillsets will be new by 2020, requiring workers to adapt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: A study says 44% of work activities in Singapore today can be automated with current technologies, with a third of the skillsets required to perform today’s jobs wholly new by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Rapid skills churn will require workers to swiftly adapt and cope with frequent career transitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am heartened that come April 2020, all transformation efforts supported by ESG’s EDG must include positive outcomes for workers, such as wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am also glad that NTUC's call for the extension of the CSP and SEC have been heeded.

sections.label: PMET share of employed residents
sections.summary: The line between rank and file and PMETs is blurred, and PMETs rose to 57% of employed residents in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: As work evolves, the line between the rank and file and PMETs is increasingly blurred, the share of PMETs among employed residents has also increased to 57% in 2018.

sections.label: Extending PWM to PMETs
sections.summary: Unions have implemented wage and skills ladders, and it is timely to extend PWM to lower-wage PMETs nationally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Beyond the mandatory PWM, our unions have been implementing structured wage and skills ladders benefiting all workers, including PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is timely to scale these efforts on a national level and extend PWM to lower-wage PMETs to provide for their progression and upward labour mobility.

sections.label: Extending schemes for ageing workforce
sections.summary: The speaker called for SEC, CSP and WorkPro to be extended and enhanced, and the Budget responded positively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To expand the potential of our ageing workforce, I have called for the SEC, CSP and WorkPro to be extended and enhanced to maximise our workforce's productive longevity and am glad that the Budget this year has responded positively.

sections.label: Top-up for individual training
sections.summary: Utilisation has increased, so a top-up of another $500 is proposed for workers' individual initiated training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Utilisation has increased and it is the time for a top-up of another $500 so that workers can go further in their personal growth through individual, initiated training.

sections.label: Worker skills upgrading and retraining
sections.summary: It states workers must have skills for these jobs and that spending on upgrading and retraining should be bolder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most importantly, we have to make sure our workers have the skills to do these jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We should be bolder in spending money on upgrading and retraining.

sections.label: Labour Movement as workers' viewfinder
sections.summary: The Labour Movement commits to be the workers' viewfinder by bringing stakeholders together to make better skills, jobs and pay real for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement is committed to serve as the workers' viewfinder in navigating the work landscape, by bringing stakeholders together to collectively make better skills, jobs and pay real for workers – I repeat, real for workers.

sections.label: Productivity increase statistic
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance shared that productivity increased 3.6% in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Having said that, the Minister for Finance has shared an encouraging statistic – productivity has increased 3.6% in the past three years.

sections.label: NTUC upstream transformation and EDG changes
sections.summary: NTUC welcomes impending changes to ESG's EDG terms, requiring companies to show initiatives benefit business and give positive worker outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With the economy transforming rapidly, if we are to help our workers upskill effectively, NTUC and our unions must now move upstream to participate in Government and industry-led transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This is why NTUC strongly welcomes the impending changes to the terms of ESG's EDG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For funding to be approved, a company must demonstrate how such initiatives not only benefit the business, but also provide positive worker outcomes.

sections.label: IGP workers and wage increases
sections.summary: As of December 2018, the IGP benefited over 91,000 workers from 2,000 companies, with average wage increase per project around 13% over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As of December 2018, the IGP has benefited more than 91,000 workers from 2,000 companies across various sectors: security guards, cleaners, F&B service staff, and hotel service staff.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the past five years, the average wage increase per project was around 13%.

sections.label: Ground work for business and training
sections.summary: They worked company by company, persuaded management that innovation and worker training would be good for business, and encouraged fellow workers to participate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: They worked the ground, company by company, to understand specific business needs and operational process details.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: They persuaded management that innovation and worker training would be good for business and encouraged their fellow workers also to participate in this upstream work to support the successes of their bosses so that, in turn, they can get better pay.

sections.label: Workers and Industry 4.0
sections.summary: Industry 4.0 requires workers to transform alongside their companies and industries, since it cannot happen without workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For Industry 4.0 to be actualised, we need our workers to transform in parallel with their companies and industries because there can be no Industry 4.0 without the workers.

sections.label: Worker 4.0 archetypes study
sections.summary: Technology can overcome labour shortage constraints, and a study with companies and sector agencies produced Worker 4.0 archetypes so workers benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Technology allows us, especially in our context, to overcome many of our labour shortage constraints and, if applied intelligently, businesses can be more productive and able to seize many emerging opportunities and create wealth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the past few months, we worked with companies and sector agencies on a study to produce archetypes of Worker 4.0 in different industries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We want workers to be able to benefit from this transformation and be assured that this is, indeed, the best for them.

sections.label: PSA Port Engineering training
sections.summary: PSA officers and the Port Officers' Union developed training programmes for Port Engineering Professional 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: As part of this study, PSA officers worked with the Port Officers' Union to develop training programmes for Port Engineering Professional 4.0.

sections.label: Training Committees with companies
sections.summary: The Labour Movement will set up Training Committees with partnering companies, including PSA among around 10 companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: To do so, the Labour Movement will work to set up Training Committees with our partnering companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: PSA, of course, is amongst a group of around 10 companies in various sectors working with our unions on their Training Committees.

sections.label: Pilot programmes reach 64,000 workers
sections.summary: The initial pilot programmes and pilot companies can reach about 64,000 workers in unionised companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With these initial pilot programmes and pilot companies, we can already reach out to about 64,000 workers in our unionised companies.

sections.label: Gainsharing and wage increases
sections.summary: Companies tapping the EDG must ensure employees benefit, such as through wage increases, and NTUC's e2i IGP has benefited over 90,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: More importantly, companies should share their successes with workers through gainsharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Therefore, they were very happy when they heard Minister Heng Swee Keat's announcement that, from next year April onwards, companies which tap on the EDG to transform must ensure that their employees also benefit, such as in the form of wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: NTUC’s e2i IGP, since was launched in 2010, has benefited more than 90,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In the past five years, the average wage increase per project was about 13%.

sections.label: Training Committees for Worker 4.0
sections.summary: Training Committees in companies are set up to help workers undergo training and upskilling to become Worker 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: To actualise the archetypes, the next step is setting up Training Committees in companies to help workers undergo training and upskilling to become Worker 4.0.

sections.label: 1969 Modernisation Seminar and tripartism
sections.summary: In 1969 the NTUC held a Modernisation Seminar during an employment crisis, generating Singapore's collaborative tripartism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In 1969, NTUC organised the "Trade Union Seminar on Modernisation of the Labour Movement" in the midst of an employment crisis when the British announced that they were pulling out of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This "Modernisation Seminar" generated Singapore's unique brand of collaborative tripartism.

sections.label: Modernisation Seminar 50th anniversary
sections.summary: Twenty-nineteen is the 50th anniversary of the Modernisation Seminar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Twenty-nineteen is the 50th anniversary of the Modernisation Seminar.

sections.label: Merdekas aged 60 to 69
sections.summary: Merdekas are aged 60 to 69, spanning ageing landmarks from the senior citizen concession card to CPF auto-payout.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today the Merdekas are aged 60 to 69 years old.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This stretches across the landmarks of ageing in Singapore, from applying for the senior citizen concession card for public transport at 60 to getting the CPF auto-payout at 70 if they had not opted for earlier payouts.

sections.label: Subsidies for Merdekas and Pioneers
sections.summary: Recognition is built into the PGP as outpatient subsidies and continued in the MGP via CHAS auto-enrolment and further subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This recognition is built into the PGP in the form of subsidies for outpatient services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This recognition is continued into the MGP with the auto-enrolment of Merdekas into the CHAS scheme and further subsidies at polyclinics and public specialist outpatient clinics, as has benefited the Pioneers.

sections.label: Call for primary care subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to commit to primary care subsidies for all subsequent generations of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, it can and should be turned into something good.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, call on the Government to commit to providing primary care subsidies for all subsequent generations of seniors, that everyone who turns 60 would be auto-enrolled in CHAS and receive additional outpatient subsidies.

sections.label: Primary care subsidies for seniors
sections.summary: The Government should make primary care subsidies compulsory for all future generations of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In return, the Government should make it compulsory that it provides for primary care subsidies for all future generations of seniors, so that we can all age with independence like the Pioneers and the Merdekas.

sections.label: Retirement age, re-employment, CPF
sections.summary: The Government is called on to remove the retirement age, move re-employment to 70, and restore older workers' CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to call on the Government to, one, remove the retirement age entirely; two, move the redefined re-employment age to 70 when employers would place able workers on rolling re-employment contracts; and three, restore the CPF contribution of older workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Doing this now that the MG is reaching the current retirement and re-employment ages of 62 and 67 is very appropriate.

sections.label: CPF monies belong to members
sections.summary: CPF monies belong to the CPF member despite employer contributions and occasional Government top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: CPF is a store of a worker's savings and is akin to a fixed deposit account.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We have to be unequivocal in stating that the monies in a CPF member's account belong to the CPF member, no fudging around this principle just because there is an employer contribution component and there are occasional Government top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our CPF savings are the fruits of our labour, period.

sections.label: Lower CPF Payout Eligibility Age
sections.summary: The Workers' Party calls to lower the CPF Payout Eligibility Age to 60 so seniors can use their own savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If their CPF Life payouts can start earlier for these seniors, their financial well-being will be secured with their own savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to reiterate the Workers' Party's call to lower the CPF Payout Eligibility Age to 60, so that Singaporeans can have the option of meeting their needs with this source of supplementary income.

sections.label: Gender gap in CPF savings
sections.summary: CareShield Life participation incentives for female seniors should be raised in proportion to the gender gap in CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
