sentences.text: In 2006, for CPF members aged 51-54, male members' Ordinary Account and Special Account balances comprised 63% of the total balances of all members, leaving female members with 37%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While the gender gap is being closed with each generation, there is an urgent need to provide extra help for Merdeka women.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We continue to call for gender-equal premiums for CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, since CareShield Life premiums are currently gender differentiated, I would like to call for the participation incentive for female seniors to enrol in CareShield Life to be raised in proportion to the gender gap in CPF savings for their generation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The MediSave top-ups for Merdeka women should also be calibrated to plug the gender gap.

sections.label: Honouring Merdeka women's sacrifices
sections.summary: More Merdeka men than women signing up for CareShield Life because of the gender gap would be a perverse outcome.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should honour these women for their sacrifices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It would be a perverse outcome that if, with the additional participation incentive in the Package, more Merdeka men than Merdeka women sign up for CareShield Life because of the gender gap.

sections.label: Calibrating policies for seniors
sections.summary: The speaker proposes calibrating healthcare, manpower, pension, housing and gender policies so seniors age with independence, listing five specific measures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We need and we should calibrate our healthcare, manpower, social pension, housing and gender policies to make sure our seniors age with independence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have made the case that: one, CHAS auto-enrollment and outpatient subsidies should kick in for all Singaporeans who turn 60 years old to plug the primary care gap in our universal healthcare system; two, the retirement age be removed, the redefined re-employment age raised to 70 years old and the CPF contribution for older workers restored so that our seniors can continue working as long as they can and want; three, CPF be transformed into a safety net for seniors, that payout eligibility age be lowered to 60 years old and members be allowed to make partial withdrawals if incapacitated to work for a period of time; four, ageing in place be deepened by promoting the Lease Buyback Scheme to the Merdekas; and five, close the gender gap in CPF and other savings for our senior women by increasing the MediSave top-ups for them and the participation incentive for them to enrol in CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If we have missed our chances with the Pioneers, we should not miss this opportunity with the Merdekas.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The MG represents the very spirit, idea and realisation of independence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We owe it to the Merdekas that they age with independence.

sections.label: Budget themes 2016 to 2018
sections.summary: It states the themes of Budget 2016, 2017 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 was "Partnering for the Future"; 2017 was "Moving Forward Together"; 2018 was "Together a Better Future".

sections.label: Diesel tax and MGP purpose
sections.summary: It cites the diesel tax doubling and reduced foreign-worker dependence, and says the $8-billion MGP's purpose is misunderstood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, the doubling of the diesel tax, introduced much to the chagrin of my colleague, Mr Ang Hin Kee, to ensure a sustainable environment; and reducing foreign-worker dependence to encourage higher productivity On the $8-billion MGP, there seems to be a misunderstanding on the purpose behind it.

sections.label: Funding MGP through Reserves
sections.summary: It says MGP can be funded through current Reserves because stamp duty and MAS contributions were higher than expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, the case for acknowledging their contributions is, therefore, strong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Now, it seems to me that we are in a fortunate situation to be able to fund MGP through the current Reserves because we have higher than expected contributions from stamp duty, as well as from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

sections.label: MGP funding quantum query
sections.summary: It says the scheme promotes an active lifestyle and healthcare subsidies, and queries $6.1 billion set aside for expected $8-billion expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is well designed to promote an active lifestyle, in addition to providing for further healthcare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do have a query on the funding quantum, though: $6.1 billion is being set aside for an expected $8-billion expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As a comparison, for the PGP, $8 billion was set aside for an expected $9-billion expenditure.

sections.label: No automatic entitlement to packages
sections.summary: It says the House should disabuse the notion that each succeeding generation is automatically entitled to a package beyond Budget needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do not have a suggestion for Assoc Prof Goh's generation, however.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is important that while we honour the MG's contributions through the MGP, we in this House also take the opportunity to disabuse the notion that each succeeding generation would be automatically entitled to a package, over and above the needs that have to be taken care of by the Budget.

sections.label: Port officers, SMEs, services quota
sections.summary: The speaker notes Port officers' upskilling for automated mega ports, support for SME programmes, and a downward adjustment of the services sector workforce quota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As advisor to the Port Officers' Union (POU), I am personally aware of the great strides made by the Port officers to be ready for the automated mega ports by upskilling themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that the hon Minister intends to provide more support and, in some instances, refinements to current programmes, such as the SME Go Digital programme and the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the same time, the hon Minister announced adjusting downwards of the workforce quota for the services sector which generates about 70% of our GDP.

sections.label: Social Ministries spending doubled
sections.summary: The Minister said social Ministries' spending doubled to $30 billion within nine years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister mentioned that the social Ministries' spending has doubled to $30 billion within a nine-year period.

sections.label: Volunteerism and Bicentennial Community Fund
sections.summary: Steps to enhance volunteerism among youths, seniors and public officers, and the Bicentennial Community Fund with matching and tax incentives, address social mobility and inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The steps to enhance the spirit of volunteerism in our youths, seniors and public officers, as well as the setting up of the Bicentennial Community Fund providing dollar-for-dollar matching and tax incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These efforts will help to address issues of social mobility and inequality that Members in this House debated passionately on not too long ago.

sections.label: SMECentres, SME fund, PCPs
sections.summary: SMECentres@SMF advise SMEs on grants; SMF awaits $200 million for SME Co-Investment Fund III and has assisted close to 1,200 workers under two PCPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our SMECentres@SMF have proven to be an effective partner to SMEs seeking customised advice and guidance on the latest Government grants, to give our SMEs better opportunities of success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We, therefore, eagerly await the additional $200 million in funding for SMEs expected to be brought in by the SME Co-Investment Fund III.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMF currently administers two types of PCPs – PCP Broad-based manufacturing and PCP-Overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am pleased to report that under these two programmes, SMF has assisted close to 1,200 workers on their professional conversion journey as at January 2019.

sections.label: Certified PMCs by SMF
sections.summary: Over 500 PMCs are currently certified by the SMF Singapore PMC Certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The total number of PMCs certified by the SMF Singapore PMC Certification (SPMCC) currently stands at over 500.

sections.label: SMF trade exhibitions 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, SMF led more than 600 enterprises in 41 trade exhibitions, securing over $222.3 million in trade sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, SMF led more than 600 enterprises to participate in 41 trade exhibitions, securing trade sales of over $222.3 million.

sections.label: ASEAN economy overtaking UK
sections.summary: ASEAN is the fifth largest economy by GDP, overtaking the UK in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: ASEAN is currently the fifth largest economy in the world by GDP, overtaking the UK in 2017.

sections.label: ASEAN middle-income class growth
sections.summary: The Asian Development Bank estimates about 65% of ASEAN's population will be middle-income by 2030, up from 29% in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, according to estimates from the Asian Development Bank, by the year 2030, about 65% of the ASEAN population will be classified as middle-income class, up from 29% in 2010.

sections.label: Foreign workforce policy reduction concerns
sections.summary: Businesses are concerned about the Foreign Workforce Policy reducing the DRC in services, though the reduction is rolled out progressively over two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Foreign Workforce Policy to reduce the DRC in the services sector is definitely something that businesses are very concerned about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses also note that the reduction is being rolled out progressively over two years to cushion the harshness of such a reduction.

sections.label: Labour shortage driving businesses out
sections.summary: A lack of readily available human resources will drive up labour costs and push businesses out of Singapore or out of business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For these businesses, no matter how technology may alleviate operational demands, a lack of readily available human resources, which will invariably in turn drive up already increasing labour costs, will work in tandem to drive businesses out of Singapore or out of business altogether.

sections.label: TACs urge flexible labour review
sections.summary: TACs will urge companies to digitalise, and ask the Ministry to consider a flexible review of labour needs closer to the cuts or case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the part of TACs, we will continue to urge companies to move towards their digitalisation journey with greater alacrity to adapt to staffing realities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as labour demands vary with each industry across different time periods, I would urge the Ministry to consider adopting a flexible policy of review, closer to when the cuts are to be made effective, or to allow flexibility to consider on a case-by-case basis, the labour needs of individual businesses.

sections.label: Support for SME digitalisation assistance
sections.summary: Businesses need assistance for changes, so the speaker supports expanding IDPs for SMEs and extending the ASP by two years, and asks about timelines and adoption rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While they appreciate the short-term sacrifices they have to make for long-term gains, and they see the need to redesign and upgrade the types of jobs to cater to a more educated ageing workforce who want to work longer in more meaningful work, they need all possible assistance to effect these changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, I fully support the Government’s decision to expand the Industry Digital Plans (IDPs) for SMEs and to extend the Automation Support Package (ASP) by two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Does the Government have a timeline for the implementation of IDPs for the remaining sectors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For the seven industries where IDPs had already been rolled out, would the Minister share an update on the adoption rate of each industry so far?

sections.label: ASP automation budget and SMEs
sections.summary: Asks whether the ASP budget to help companies scale up automation was fully used yearly since 2016, and how many SMEs and sectors it helped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As for ASP, I would like to ask if the amount budgeted to assist companies to scale up their automation projects had been fully utilised each year since it was launched in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How many SMEs has ASP helped and in which sectors?

sections.label: CPF interest for low balances
sections.summary: Calls for higher tiered CPF interest rates for Singaporeans with low CPF balances, noting existing extra interest tiers and Budget top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In line with the Government's targeted mode to help the most vulnerable, I would like to reiterate my call for more help for Singaporeans with low CPF balances, such as the group with balances below the Basic Retirement Sum, through higher tiered CPF interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is in addition to the current Budget top-up of $300-$1,000 for older Singaporeans with low CPF balances and, from time to time, when we have surpluses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On the first $60,000 of a CPF member's combined balances, with up to $20,000 from the Ordinary Account (OA), an extra 1% interest is paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Since January 2016, CPF members aged 55 and above will also earn an additional 1% extra interest on the first $30,000 of their combined balances, including up to $20,000 from the OA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These extra interests apply on the first $60,000 and first $30,000 respectively, regardless of whether one has a combined CPF savings of $60,000 or $600,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will consider increasing the additional interest for those who have low combined CPF balances, for example, below the Basic Retirement Sum, to help them earn more in their accounts.

sections.label: Economic prosperity through SMEs
sections.summary: States that economic prosperity continues through the uplifting of SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: First, the continuation of our economic prosperity through the uplifting of our SMEs.

sections.label: Orchard Pig turnover
sections.summary: States that Orchard Pig's success led to a £6 million turnover in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Orchard Pig’s success led to a £6 million turnover in 2018.

sections.label: Eco-friendly building tax rebates
sections.summary: Suggests tax rebates for eco-friendly building standards, materials and efficient utility consumption, citing the BCA Green Mark Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: There are frameworks that assess the eco-friendliness of buildings, such as the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) Green Mark Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I believe eco-friendliness can be promoted by introducing tax rebates for compliance with eco-friendly building standards, use of eco-friendly building materials, and efficient consumption of utilities.

sections.label: SEC green labelling results
sections.summary: States that 40 certified buildings cut electricity use by 20.1 million kWh and CO2 emissions by 66,120 tonnes, and that the SEC scheme is ISO-recognised in 43 countries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The results are impressive: seven years since its inception, 40 buildings certified under this scheme contributed to reduced electricity consumption of 20.1 million kilowatt-hours (kWh), and reduced carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions of 66,120 tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The SEC’s green labelling scheme is internationally recognised under the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 17065 and ISO 14024 for certifying products which meet stringent environmental standards and is accepted in 43 countries.

sections.label: Tokyo Vision and Olympics
sections.summary: Tokyo's 2014 plan aims to make Tokyo the world's best city, using the Olympics to gain renown for arts and culture.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Tokyo Government formulated a plan in 2014 with the explicit aim of making Tokyo the world's best city known as "The Tokyo Vision".

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: One of their strategies involves the use of the Olympics as the platform by which Tokyo may become world-renowned for arts and culture, which, in turn, set Tokyo on the path to becoming a world-leading cultural city.

sections.label: Tokyo foreign city relations
sections.summary: The Tokyo Vision includes developing relations with 30 foreign cities, blurring federal and city governance lines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As part of The Tokyo Vision, the Tokyo government will develop relations with 30 foreign cities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This has resulted in the blurring of lines between federal and city governance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have strong ties with other federal Governments, and learnt and shared much with them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We should expand our networks with city and municipal governments so that our 3P sectors can learn and share their respective experiences.

sections.label: British defeat by Japan
sections.summary: It asks how the British, after 20 years of planning Singapore's defence with 130,000 troops, could be defeated by a Japanese army about one third its size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How could the British, after 20 years of planning for Singapore's defence, with an army of 130,000 troops, be defeated by a Japanese army of roughly one third its size?

sections.label: Singapore naval base approval
sections.summary: In 1921 the British cabinet approved building a new naval base out of Singapore to host its main fleet in a future world war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the event of a future world war, Britain will concentrate its entire navy to defeat its European enemies, and then sail the main fleet down to Singapore to counter the Japanese.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, in 1921, the British cabinet approved the building of a new naval base out of Singapore to host its main fleet.

sections.label: Singapore base fleet capacity
sections.summary: The British knew they needed most or all of their fleet against Japan, but Singapore's naval base was never designed to hold more than 20% of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The British knew they need most, if not all, of their fleet to contend with the Japanese.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But surprisingly, the naval base in Singapore was never designed to hold more than 20% of its fleet.

sections.label: Singapore Strategy strategic illusion
sections.summary: The Singapore Strategy was a "Strategic Illusion", a plan that could never work against a determined enemy and one hopes will never be tested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In short, the Singapore Strategy was nothing more than a "Strategic Illusion", a plan that could never work against a determined enemy, a plan one hopes will never be tested.

sections.label: British surrender after seven-day fight
sections.summary: After a seven-day fight for Singapore, the divided and demoralised British army, still 100,000 men strong, chose to surrender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After a seven-day fight for Singapore, the divided and demoralised British army, still 100,000 men strong, chose to surrender.

sections.label: Defence budget and deterrence
sections.summary: Advanced militaries face challenges like fifth generation aerial, cyber and hybrid warfare and disruptive drones and AI, so 30% of the Budget goes to defence, security and diplomacy as there is no substitute to deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The most advanced militaries today grapple with major challenges, such as adapting to fifth generation aerial warfare, contending with cyber and hybrid warfare, dealing with disruptive innovations from drones to AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am heartened that 30% of our Budget this year goes to defence, security and diplomacy, because history shows there is no substitute to deterrence.

sections.label: GDP, unemployment, inflation, wages
sections.summary: The past year's GDP growth is strong, unemployment and inflation are both low, and median wage increases are high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The past year's GDP growth is strong, unemployment and inflation are both low, and median wage increases are high.

sections.label: Fiscal discipline and Reserves
sections.summary: Voices ask for more spending and Reserve income, but Reserves must anchor the economy, and rising non-discretionary spending leaves less room to build a better Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On maintaining our fiscal discipline, there are many voices asking for more Government spending, and to dig deeper into our Reserve income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But our Reserves must anchor our economy through turbulent times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the same time, in this House, we frequently say that we are not done building Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But as non-discretionary spending forms a larger percentage of our Budget, there is less room for major shifts to respond to a changing world, less room to build a better Singapore across generations.

sections.label: Five proposals for seniors
sections.summary: Five proposals cover automatic CHAS and outpatient treatment at 60, abolishing retirement age and raising re-employment to 70, lowering CPF withdrawal age to 60, promoting Lease Buyback for the Merdeka Generation, and MediSave top-ups for female seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, automatic registration for CHAS subsidies and also outpatient treatment for all Singaporeans once they reach 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, abolish the retirement age, increase the re-employment age to 70 and restore the CPF contributions for older workers so that our seniors can continue to work as long as they wish to and are able to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, transform the CPF into a safety net for seniors whereby the eligible withdrawal age, or the age when they are eligible to receive payouts, is lowered to 60 and members are allowed to make partial withdrawals from the available sum if they are unable to work for a certain period of time due to health issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fourth, strengthen ageing further by promoting HDB's Lease Buyback Scheme to the Merdeka Generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifth and finally, address the gender gap for CPF and other savings for our female seniors by increasing the amount of MediSave top-ups for this group and also provide incentives for participation so that they will register for CareShield Life.

sections.label: Cross-cultural, digital, ethical literacies
sections.summary: The speaker says that if the Annual Budget starts with A and B, he will speak about literacies beginning with C, D and E: cross-cultural literacy, digital literacy and ethical literacy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the Annual Budget starts with A and B, I would like to speak today about literacies beginning with C, D and E.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are cross-cultural literacy, digital literacy and ethical literacy.

sections.label: Cross-cultural literacy defined
sections.summary: Cross-cultural literacy is the ability to understand and interact across cultures sensitively and respectfully of diversity.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Cross-cultural literacy is the ability to understand and interact across different cultures in a manner that is sensitive to differences, yet respectful of diversity.

sections.label: Digital access and skills divides
sections.summary: Schemes have given Singaporeans basic digital access, but emerging skills divides need targeted support for specific groups.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Schemes, such as the National Education University (NEU) Personal Computer (PC) Plus and Home Access programmes for low-income households, and Enable information technology (IT) for persons with disabilities, have helped to make sure that all Singaporeans have basic access to digital technology.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, we must be vigilant about any emerging digital skills divides that may find certain segments of our population less advantaged and less able to benefit from our digitalisation push.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the Ministry of Communications and Information's Digital Readiness Blueprint and its recommendation that all citizens be equipped with a foundational set of digital skills.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Going beyond the Basic Digital Skills Curriculum, however, we need to pay particular attention to providing support for specific demographic groups that may require more targeted assistance.

sections.label: Ethical literacy for workforce
sections.summary: Growing digitalisation requires enhancing the workforce's ethical literacy to recognise and resolve ethical issues.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because our society is becoming more digitalised, with a growing embrace of the Internet of Things, Big Data, AI, machine learning and automation, we must enhance the ethical literacy of our workforce to ensure that these technologies are deployed in the best interests of our society.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, we must vest our workforce with the competencies to recognise ethical issues where and when they present themselves, understand different ethical perspectives and to apply these perspectives to help resolve ethical conundrums.

sections.label: Big Tech ethical controversies
sections.summary: Big Tech controversies show inattention to ethics causes problems, making the Proposed Model AI Governance Framework farsighted and commendable.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Controversies in Big Tech have shown how inattention to ethical considerations can lead to issues, such as Facebook's Cambridge Analytica debacle and Uber using its technology to track users’ locations against their will.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Proposed Model AI Governance Framework launched in January is both farsighted and commendable.

sections.label: Budget and fiscal approach
sections.summary: The Budget takes a counter-cyclical approach with measures to boost competitiveness and skills despite moving from surplus to deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The best way to go about this is to continue growing the economy, keep a broad-based tax, have a diverse source of revenue and maintain fiscal prudence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that for this year's Budget, the Government has taken a counter-cyclical approach by introducing multifaceted measures to boost competitiveness, productivity and to upskill and reskill and rightskill workers, despite going from a surplus of $2.1 billion, or 0.4% of GDP in FY2018, to a deficit of $3.5 billion, or 0.7% of GDP in FY2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is, indeed, a generous and ambitious Budget, in my opinion, with special transfers rising to $15.3 billion, up from $9 billion in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is the highest special transfer on record above the $12.4 billion in Budget FY2014 when the PG package was unveiled.

sections.label: Fiscal policy and safety net
sections.summary: Fiscal policy facilitates more equitable redistribution, with enhanced transfers and long-term commitments forming a vital safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This means that in recognising the economic realities of uneven distribution of resources, fiscal policy is meant to facilitate a slightly more equitable redistribution of resources across the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, we are seeing further enhancements to fiscal transfer packages, such as the ComCare Long-term Assistance, and WIS, alongside longer-term commitments, such as the $6.1 billion MGP and $5.1 billion in long-term care support initiatives, to form a vital safety net.

sections.label: Available programmes for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage lists KidSTART, Global Ready Infrastructure Talent, SkillsFuture, Adapt and Grow, PCPs, and career guidance and counselling as available programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: KidSTART, Global Ready Infrastructure Talent, SkillsFuture, Adapt and Grow, PCPs, career guidance and counselling are just a few of the available programmes one can tap on.

sections.label: Enhancing segment of post-secondary cohort
sections.summary: The passage states this segment is 25%-30% of the post-secondary cohort yearly and a significant future labour force with key skillsets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, we will have to focus more to continue enhancing it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This segment constitutes 25%-30% of the post-secondary cohort each year and is a significant future labour force with key skillsets for us to be future-ready.

sections.label: SEN support at ITE
sections.summary: The passage asks about allocating more resources to ITE's SEN support office, noting these students are about 4% of ITE enrolment and about 2,500 SEN students enrolled in IHLs over three decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But can we allocate more resources to the ITE to help enhance the Special Educational Needs (SEN) support office?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These students account for about 4% of ITE's enrolment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On average, over the last three decades, about 2,500 students with SEN were enrolled in IHLs.

sections.label: Overseas work and GRIT programmes
sections.summary: The passage notes the Minister's promise to prepare Singaporeans for international collaboration and overseas work experience, and describes GRIT under the PCP and the new GRTP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am also pleased to note that the Minister has promised that more will be done to prepare and develop Singaporeans to seize opportunities for international collaboration and to provide more opportunities for Singaporeans to gain overseas working experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There is the Global-Ready Infrastructure Talent Programme (GRIT) under the PCP, which seeks to reskill local mid-career switchers and displaced professionals to embark on job functions required for global infrastructure projects in areas like Transaction Advisory, Project Financing, Legal Advisory and Infrastructure Engineering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Minister has revealed plans for more funding for students at IHLs who plan to intern overseas with Singaporean firms through the new Global Ready Talent Programme (GRTP).

sections.label: National savings bond suggestion
sections.summary: The passage says money is not freely withdrawn, expects hesitation to deposit more, and hopes the Government considers a national savings bond and a minimum $500 Singapore Savings Bond allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Moreover, this money is not to be freely withdrawn, so hesitation to deposit more money in the accounts is to be expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will in future consider offering a national savings bond, with a guaranteed positive real rate of interest on savings, with a maximum holding per person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government could consider allocating a minimum $500 allocation of the existing Singapore Savings Bond to every Singaporean adult.

sections.label: Funding efforts and infrastructure borrowing
sections.summary: The passage states the urgent question of sustainably funding efforts, and notes the Minister's plans for huge infrastructure projects partly funded through borrowing and embedded Government guarantees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even as we discuss the possible enhancements for the various schemes and future Budgets, we cannot avoid the increasingly urgent question of how to sustainably fund all these efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that the Minister has plans for huge infrastructure projects and other infrastructure investments to be partly funded through borrowing and embedded Government guarantees.

sections.label: Millennials worse off than parents
sections.summary: Researchers and economists presented financial reports showing millennials are doing worse off than their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, researchers from the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), along with economists from Stanford University, Harvard University and the University of California at Berkeley, presented financial reports and comparisons indicating that millennials are doing worse off than their parents.

sections.label: Wealth-based tax tiers
sections.summary: A wealth-based tax may be more pertinent, with different tiers of taxes possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Some sort of wealth-based tax may be more pertinent, and we could have different tiers of taxes.

sections.label: Diesel excise duty increase
sections.summary: In Budget 2019, Minister Heng Swee Keat announced diesel excise duty rose from $0.10 to $0.20 per litre immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Does the Budget this year help to build that resiliency?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We see elements of this in Budget 2019 where Minister Heng Swee Keat announced that the excise duty on diesel fuel has been increased from $0.10 to $0.20 per litre with immediate effect.

sections.label: Road tax rebates offset
sections.summary: Announced road tax rebates for commercial diesel vehicles will not completely offset excise tax payable according to usage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The announced road tax rebates for commercial diesel vehicles are not going to completely offset the excise tax payable according to usage.

sections.label: Changi East borrowing guarantee
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat said Changi Airport Group will take loans for Changi East, with Government guaranteeing borrowings to reduce cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In his Budget speech last week, Minister Heng Swee Keat mentioned that for the development of Changi East, where the new Terminal 5 (T5) will be built, the Changi Airport Group will be taking loans to fund its share of the infrastructure and the Government will provide a guarantee for the Changi East borrowings in order to reduce the cost of borrowing.

sections.label: Malaysia taking back Johor airspace
sections.summary: On 4 December 2018 Malaysia announced intentions to take back delegated airspace in southern Johor, which Singapore has provided air traffic control for since 1974.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On 4 December 2018, Malaysia announced its intentions to take back its delegated airspace in southern Johor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore has been providing air traffic control services over southern Johor through the Operational Letter of Agreement Between Kuala Lumpur and Singapore Area Control Centres Concerning Singapore Arrivals, Departures and Overflight since 1974.

sections.label: Malaysia port limit boundary dispute
sections.summary: Malaysia unilaterally attempted to draw a new port limit boundary off Tuas in November last year, encroaching on Singapore's waters, with the standoff continuing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In November last year, Malaysia unilaterally attempted to draw a new port limit boundary off Tuas, encroaching on the waters which have long been under the jurisdiction and control of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The standoff has continued since November 2018, and the Malaysian government vessels have remained in our port waters since.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There was even a collision in those waters between a Malaysian government vessel and a tanker, bringing with it awkward issues of jurisdiction exercised by both port authorities for the investigation of liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our port waters, being filled with so many visiting and passing vessels, are already bursting at its seams and being sandwiched between the Malaysian and Indonesian waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am concerned how the latest developments may affect our port or ancillary maritime businesses, whether in the short or longer run, if this is not managed and resolved appropriately by our Government in our negotiations with Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In January this year, Mr Andreas Sohmen-Pao, Chairman, Singapore Maritime Foundation, said at the Singapore Maritime Foundation (SMF) New Year Cocktail Reception that "just as shipping fundamentals are starting to look a little better, we see new issues around geopolitics, trade policies, energy and equity market volatility which have us wondering whether the long-awaited improvements will materialise after all." In my Budget Debate speech last year, I said that while I support the push for digitalisation and innovation under the Sea Transport ITM, we must not forget those who may not be able to benefit from this development.

sections.label: Proposals for seniors' healthcare and CPF
sections.summary: Five proposals: CHAS auto-enrolment at 60, removing retirement age, transforming CPF into a safety net, promoting Lease Buyback, and closing the gender CPF gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, CHAS auto-enrolment and outpatient subsidies should kick in for all Singaporeans who turn 60 years old to plug the primary care gap in our universal healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, the retirement age be removed, re-employment age raised to 70 and CPF contribution for older workers restored so that our seniors can continue working as long as they can and want to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Third, CPF be transformed into a safety net for seniors, that payout eligibility age be lowered to 60 and members be allowed to make partial withdrawals if incapacitated to work for a period of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourth, ageing in place be deepened by promoting the Lease Buyback Scheme to the Merdekas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fifth, close the gender gap in CPF and other savings for our senior women by increasing the MediSave top-ups for them and the participation incentive for them to enrol in CareShield Life.

sections.label: Tightening Services sector Dependency Ratio Ceiling
sections.summary: The Government had to make the difficult decision of tightening the Dependency Ratio Ceiling and S Pass sub-DRC for the Services sector in 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Today, I will explain why the Government had to make the difficult decision of tightening the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) and the S Pass sub-DRC for the Services sector in 2020 and 2021.

sections.label: Increase in Services sector work pass holders
sections.summary: The number of S Pass and Work Permit holders in the Services sector has increased by 34,000 in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The number of S Pass and Work Permit holders in the Services sector has increased by 34,000 in the last three years.

sections.label: Productivity growth by industry
sections.summary: Real value-added per actual hour worked from 2013 to 2018 rose 4.4% per annum for accommodation, 3.2% for retail trade and 1.4% for food services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If we look at the real value-added per actual hour worked from 2013 to 2018, which is one measure of productivity, it has increased by 4.4% per annum for the accommodation industry, 3.2% per annum for retail trade and 1.4% per annum for food services.

sections.label: Enhanced Productivity Solutions Grant training subsidy
sections.summary: The Productivity Solutions Grant will be enhanced to include a new subsidy of up to $10,000 for employer-led training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, we will be enhancing the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) to include a new subsidy of up to $10,000 for employer-led training.

sections.label: Business forms and licensing review
sections.summary: A pilot system launches in May after consolidating forms, cutting data fields, fees and processing time, with rules review ongoing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will be launching the pilot system for beta-testing in May.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: So far, we have managed to consolidate the number of forms that businesses need to submit from 14 to 1, reduced the number of data fields required from 845 to 130, slashed licensing fees by up to $500, and shortened the processing time by two weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: My colleagues and I are working hard on rules review because we believe it supports entrepreneurship and innovation, which are critical elements to achieve our economic transformation goals.

sections.label: Ngee Soon RFID stocktaking
sections.summary: In 2014 Ngee Soon implemented an RFID system that cut daily stocktaking time by more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2014, Ngee Soon implemented a Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) system, which allowed them to reduce the amount of time taken for daily stocktaking by more than 50%.

sections.label: Companies transforming with Government support
sections.summary: All companies must transform to increase competitiveness, and Government and industry associations will walk this journey with them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: All companies, no matter big or small, modern or traditional, have to transform to increase their competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government and industry associations will walk this journey together with our companies.

sections.label: Response to Workers' Party MPs
sections.summary: The speaker says he will now respond to some points from the Workers' Party Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, I would now like to respond to some of the points from the Workers' Party Members of Parliament.

sections.label: Universal healthcare insurance premiums
sections.summary: This universal healthcare insurance protects Singaporeans against large hospital bills, with premium subsidies and support for low- and middle-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is part of the primary care network that Mr Pritam Singh and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh spoke about.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is a universal healthcare insurance that protects Singaporeans against large hospital bills, with premium subsidies and additional premium support from Government to help low-income Singaporeans and middle-income Singaporeans pay for their premiums.

sections.label: CHAS subsidies and enhanced coverage
sections.summary: In 2017 more than 650,000 Singaporeans benefited from $154 million of CHAS subsidies, and coverage and benefits will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2017 – and this is before the enhancement – more than 650,000 Singaporeans benefited from $154 million of CHAS subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And we will enhance the coverage, we will enhance the help that Singaporeans can get, the benefits that Singaporeans can get under CHAS, as part of enhancing primary care, and giving Singaporeans greater peace of mind.

sections.label: Funds from Budget surpluses
sections.summary: Funds are set aside from current Budget surpluses to give MGs peace of mind and encourage them to stay active and healthy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As previously explained, we are setting aside funds from current Budget surpluses to give our MGs greater peace of mind and encourage them to stay active and stay healthy.

sections.label: Earning surpluses during term
sections.summary: Surpluses are derived by earning them during the term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The way we derive the surpluses is that you have to earn these surpluses during the term of Government.

sections.label: Universal versus cohort-based schemes
sections.summary: Some asked whether cohort-based PGP and MGP can be replaced by a permanent universal system; he can support one if resources are available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Some in this House have asked whether cohort-based schemes like the PGP and MGP can be replaced by a more permanent universal system, a permanent system that automatically gives subsidy based on a certain age, like our transport concession for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In principle, if resources are available for the long haul, I can support a universal scheme that automatically distributes the benefits of the package to all above 60.

sections.label: Universal scheme less targeted
sections.summary: A universal scheme will be more blunt, broad-based and less targeted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A universal scheme will be more blunt, broad-based and less targeted.

sections.label: Financing cohort versus permanent schemes
sections.summary: A cohort-based scheme is financed by the current Government without burdening future generations, while a permanent scheme needs additional recurrent funding future governments may not cope with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A cohort-based scheme is financed by the current Government and does not burden our future generations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A permanent scheme will need additional recurrent funding which future governments may not be able to cope.

sections.label: MOE Kindergarten fees and preschool
sections.summary: A four-hour MOE Kindergarten programme costs parents $160 monthly; he hopes preschool education is made compulsory with more resources so fees can be free.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In contrast, a four-hour Ministry of Education (MOE) Kindergarten programme will cost parents $160 per month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: All educators know the importance of early childhood education as it sets the foundation for the child.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government or the future government will make preschool or early childhood education compulsory and provide more resources so the school fees can be free, just like for primary school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider putting more resources into SkillsFuture and top-up the accounts of Singaporeans who have utilised or exhausted their credits?

sections.label: Legally binding emissions target
sections.summary: The Act set a legally binding, scientifically informed target of an 80% emissions cut by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Act set a scientifically informed, long-term target of an 80% cut in emissions by 2050, which is legally binding.

sections.label: Proposed Climate Change Act
sections.summary: The speaker proposes enacting a Climate Change Act to show and enshrine commitment to mitigate climate change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To show and enshrine our commitment to mitigate Climate Change, I propose we enact a Climate Change Act.

sections.label: Singapore wealth inequality evidence
sections.summary: Singapore is said to have done well, but over the last decade wealth inequality increased more than income inequality.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Looking at where Singapore is, one can say that Singapore should be considered having done well as our system is built on principles of meritocracy, has a fair and progressive tax system and the redistribution of wealth has a focus on social outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But over the last decade, there is evidence that indicates that the increase in wealth inequality has become greater than income inequality.

sections.label: Charitable foundations after estate duty
sections.summary: Since estate duty was scrapped in 2008, the number of charitable foundations and trust funds increased threefold.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I believe many donate as they believe in the causes and not because of the tax deductibles.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But it is also true that since the estate duty was scrapped in 2008, the number of charitable foundations and trust funds set up has since increased three folds.

sections.label: Net wealth and inheritance tax
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a net wealth tax and inheritance tax should be considered for ultra-high net worth individuals.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While we look ahead and review the current tax system in its entirety, should we consider the possibility of a net wealth tax and inheritance tax for the ultra-high net worth individuals who make up 1%-2% of our society?

sections.label: Support for low-income workers
sections.summary: The question remains whether PWM and WIS are sufficient to meet low-income workers' and families' basic needs today.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While the current Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme are designed to help raise their wages, the question still remains whether this is sufficient in today’s context to support and meet the basic needs of the low-income workers and their families.

sections.label: Donations, basic needs, living wage
sections.summary: The passage asks whether safety nets meet basic needs and how much more consumers and employers will pay for a living wage.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Clearly, all donations will help them in one way or the other, but are these safety nets the answer to their basic needs?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Not having time only to live hand to mouth will also allow them to have some quality time with their children or grandchildren that can foster the growth of the next generation and instil family bonding that many average families enjoy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This brings us to the crux of the issue – how much more are consumers and employers willing to pay them to meet the living wage?

sections.label: Baby Boomer retirement, knowledge transfer
sections.summary: The passage states that retiring Baby Boomers and incoming millennials will cause a drain of expertise without early transfer channels.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In the next two decades, we will see the retirement of a large cohort of Baby Boomers, and the millennials will eventually make up most of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This drain of expertise and knowledge will have its repercussions if there are no early channels for inter-generation or inter-workplace transfer.

sections.label: SMEs, guidance, generational knowledge
sections.summary: The passage says startups and SMEs need knowledge and guidance from today's 40s to 50s workers and must train and rotate staff.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: For young startups and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to scale up or internationalise, they require some of this knowledge and stepping stones that can reduce their learning curve.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Consultation and guidance from the working group in their 40s to 50s today will be useful for these companies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: They must be willing to conduct inhouse development training for their workers and bridge the generational gap and workplace knowledge through job rotations and have a healthy mix in the retention of seniors.

sections.label: MediShield Life payout case
sections.summary: The passage cites MediShield Life paying out only $4.50 of a senior citizen's post-subsidy bill of nearly $4,500.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, the case of MediShield Life paying out only $4.50 of a senior citizen’s post-subsidy bill which amounted to nearly $4,500.

sections.label: MediShield Life claim limits review
sections.summary: The passage states MOH promised to review MediShield Life insurance claim limits and that this is how the matter should be handled.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: MOH has also promised to review the MediShield Life insurance claim limits, and this is how the matter should be handled.

sections.label: Water cost, retirement age, clarification
sections.summary: The passage notes water costs $2 yearly, the Retirement Sum Scheme payout age is 65, and Minister Josephine Teo clarified questions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is despite the Government’s efforts to communicate this over the past many years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It costs us $2 per year to drink two litres of water – clean safe drinking water that flows out of our taps 365 days a year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Today, the payout eligibility age for the Retirement Sum Scheme is still 65 for those born from 1954 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: But for people to think that the Government can secretly change the age shows that some people, and I hope is a minority, do not follow the news or tend to think the worst of our Government.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am glad my Parliamentary colleagues filed many questions on this, and Minister Josephine Teo has clarified.

sections.label: Earning people's trust and confidence
sections.summary: The speaker says trust comes from delivering for the people, accountability, transparency and consistent communication, and hopes his grandmother's words resonate with younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, there is simply no shortcut to earning the people's trust and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The key ingredients are delivering for the people, having accountability and transparency, as well as being consistent in our communication across the board.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I started my speech by recounting what my grandmother said many years ago, "You have no idea how important government is.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is the best Government in the world.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: They have taken care of us." I hope, and I am optimistic, that what she said then will continue to resonate with younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: With this Budget, let us persist and continue to work together for our people and our country, and do our part in co-creating the future we want for ourselves and our children.

sections.label: BCA approval for non-structural building works
sections.summary: A 2014 BCA circular required approval of building plans before non-structural works, replacing the earlier preliminary plan and Qualified Person's undertaking, typically delaying projects for months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: On 13 March 2014, BCA issued a circular to inform building industry players that they would have to obtain approval of building plans before commencing non-structural building works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Non-structural building works include building of walls and partitions so that contractors can install pipes and wires early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Prior to 2014, contractors could start non-structural work with a good preliminary building plan and a Qualified Person's (QP's) undertaking to comply with the building codes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The new requirement to obtain approval of the full building plan which has to incorporate approvals from various authorities like the National Environment Agency (NEA), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the National Parks Board (NParks), typically would delay the project for months.

sections.label: LTA safety items for motor traders
sections.summary: LTA requires motor traders to input 52 safety items into its system, while Hong Kong requires only 26 items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, LTA requires motor traders to input 52 safety items into LTA's system while our closest competitor, Hong Kong needs only 26 items.

sections.label: PUB permit for River Hongbao fireworks
sections.summary: A PUB executive refused to issue the fireworks permit as late as a fortnight before the River Hongbao opening ceremony, by which time 100,000 tickets had been issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For some reasons, this year, a PUB executive refused to issue the permit for the fireworks as late as a fortnight before the opening ceremony of the River Hongbao at which the Prime Minster was the Guest-of-Honour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: By that time, the interest in the River Hongbao fireworks was so strong that we had already issued 100,000 fireworks tickets.

sections.label: Appeal and record River Hongbao attendance
sections.summary: The speaker appealed to someone in the House, PUB approved within a day, and River Hongbao had record attendance that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Fortunately, I had someone in the House that I could appeal to and we received approval from PUB within a day of the appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As a result, we had record attendance at the River Hongbao this year.

sections.label: Productivity and Innovation Credit scheme abuse
sections.summary: The speaker says earlier action might have prevented large-scale abuse of the 2010 PIC scheme, and IRAS prosecuted 13 cases involving 37 claims worth $804,756 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Had this been done earlier, schemes like the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme launched in 2010 to encourage businesses to invest in productivity and innovation, might not have been abused to such a large extent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2018, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) said it prosecuted 13 cases involving 37 claims amounting to $804,756 of PIC cash payouts and this could be just the tip of the iceberg.

sections.label: Public-private work exchanges
sections.summary: Private sector workers can better appreciate regulations and help Government design incentives; exchanges last one to two years for promising middle management staff, citing a Sport Singapore posting to the Volleyball Association.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The private sector workers can better appreciate the need for regulations, understand the complexity of taking into account the interests of various parties and help the Government to better design incentives to shape the behaviour of the private companies in the industry transformation journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These work exchanges could last for one to two years, and the staff who are selected should be promising staff at the middle management level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, a staff from Sport Singapore, which oversees the National Sports Associations (NSAs), was posted to work as a General Manager in the Volleyball Association, not to clean up the mess, just to be sure, but to develop the sport in the volleyball fraternity.

sections.label: Structured public-private exchange programme
sections.summary: The Head of the Civil Service can consider a more structured, scalable and sustainable programme for work exchanges between the public and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Head of the Civil Service can consider a more structured, scalable and sustainable programme for such work exchanges between the public and private sectors.

sections.label: Simplifying food industry regulations
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat indicated yesterday he would lead efforts to simplify regulations in the food industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For that matter, I am pleased that Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat had indicated yesterday that he would be leading efforts to simplify the regulations in the food industry.

sections.label: Enhanced WIS, SEC payouts
sections.summary: Enhanced WIS helps more lower-wage earners with higher annual payout; SEC and Additional SEC continue helping business owners employ older Singaporeans until end of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Enhanced WIS will go some way in helping even more lower-wage income earners with a higher annual payout.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, the Special Employment Credit (SEC) and Additional SEC will continue to help business owners employ older Singaporeans until end of 2020.

sections.label: SEC for special needs workers
sections.summary: SEC and Additional SEC should also be extended to help business owners employ those with special needs and mental health challenges who may need time to adjust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The SEC and Additional SEC should also be extended in helping business owners employ those with special needs and those with mental health challenges who may need time and space to adjust to their work environments and work commitments.

sections.label: Effectiveness of PCP, CSP
sections.summary: While supporting funding for enhanced PCP and CSP, the member asks how effective PCP, Career Trial, CSP and Adapt and Grow have been in helping PMEs secure employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I support the funding for the enhanced Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) and Career Support Programme (CSP) to continue, I would like to find out how effective have our PCP, Career Trial, CSP, and Adapt and Grow Programme been in helping PMEs secure employment?

sections.label: Diesel tax cuts, electric vehicles
sections.summary: Speaker supports Budget's diesel tax reductions and rebates, and asks whether road taxes and rebates will also be lowered for electric vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also fully support the Budget’s focus on Ensuring a Sustainable Environment, particularly in reducing taxes for diesel cars and taxis, and providing higher rebates for diesel vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, are there plans to lower road taxes for electric vehicles and providing similar rebates for owners of electric vehicles which are much more environmentally friendly with zero carbon emissions?

sections.label: Budget aid and overseas work
sections.summary: Budget gives assistance to many groups and generous support to entrepreneurs expanding abroad, and speaker hopes young Malays use the Global-Ready Talent Programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   This year's Budget includes assistance for various groups and different segments of society, be it workers, employers, those who are disadvantaged, students, elderly Singaporeans and those who belong to MG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, this year's Budget allocates funds and incentives that are rather generous to support entrepreneurs who are expanding their enterprise or businesses across the border, whether in Southeast Asia or globally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, through schemes like the "Global-Ready Talent Programme", I also hope that our young Malays will seize the opportunity to experience working overseas even though it involves some personal sacrifice by being far away from their families for a period of time.

sections.label: WIS, SEC and special needs hiring
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes extended WIS and SEC aid for lower-wage and elderly workers, and asks Government to extend schemes to employers hiring special needs individuals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, I welcome the extension of assistance programmes and schemes like the enhanced WIS and SEC that will help lower-wage workers as well as elderly workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, I would also like to call on the Government to extend these assistance programmes or employment schemes to employers to encourage them to employ special needs individuals, for instance, those who have physical disabilities, autism or Down's Syndrome, as well as those who have mental health challenges.

sections.label: Streaming and social stratification
sections.summary: Streaming is named as something that might prevent social mixing and harden social stratification in secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One of the things that might prevent social mixing and harden social stratification in our secondary schools is the practice of streaming.

sections.label: Socio-economic status and PSLE streaming
sections.summary: Ong Ye Kung said socio-economic status correlates with PSLE results; Normal stream students tend to have lower status, and 69% of MOE aid recipients from 2014-2018 were Normal stream.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung has stated, "Social economic status has become significantly correlated with Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) results." The reality is that students in the Normal stream tend to have a lower socio-economic status, as compared to those from the Express stream.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We know that from 2014 to 2018, 69% of secondary school students who received assistance from the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme were from the Normal stream.

sections.label: Normal to Express stream movement
sections.summary: Only 10 to 20 of these students eventually move on to the Express stream.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Of these students, only 10 to 20 of them eventually move on to the Express stream.

sections.label: Normal (Technical) graduates in polytechnics
sections.summary: Over three years, Normal (Technical) graduates were 5% of public polytechnic graduates and 1% of autonomous university graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, Normal (Technical) graduates have made up only 5% of those who graduated from our public polytechnics and only 1% of those who graduated from our autonomous universities.

sections.label: Subject-Based Banding replacing primary streaming
sections.summary: In 2008, MOE replaced primary school streaming with Subject-Based Banding, keeping the good parts of streaming and cutting the bad parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2008, MOE listened to these concerns and replaced primary school streaming with Subject-Based Banding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Subject-Based Banding kept the good parts of streaming while cutting out the bad parts.

sections.label: Subject-Based Banding in secondary schools
sections.summary: The reasons for replacing primary streaming with Subject-Based Banding should apply to secondary schools, and Subject-Based Banding has been expanded to all secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would seem strange that we did away with streaming and adopted Subject-Based Banding in primary schools for very good reasons but somehow these reasons do not apply to secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have already expanded Subject-Based Banding to all secondary schools to benefit more students.

sections.label: School reports higher attendance rates
sections.summary: In 2018, the school reported the new system increased attendance rates and drew a positive student response, and the speaker hopes MOE studies this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2018, the school reported that the new system has led to an increase in attendance rates and was met with a positive response by the students, and I hope that MOE can study what this school has done.

sections.label: Replacing secondary streaming with Subject-Based Banding
sections.summary: The speaker urges completely replacing streaming with Subject-Based Banding in secondary schools, calling it time to slay this sacred cow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Like our primary schools, let us completely replace streaming with Subject-Based Banding in our secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Members of this House will know that I do not like to cull animals but, Sir, it is time to slain this sacred cow.

sections.label: Milanovic study on globalisation and income
sections.summary: Branko Milanovic studied income distribution from 1988 to 2008 and concluded globalisation brought divergent real income changes, with winners and losers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: World Bank economist Branko Milanovic studied the distribution of incomes across the world as globalisation took root over a 20-year period from 1988 to 2008.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He concludes that, for individuals, globalisation has brought about divergent changes in real income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The "winners" included the bottom third of income earners, the middle classes of the emerging market economies in China, India and Indonesia, and the global top 1%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The "losers" were the middle class of the old OECD countries, and the poorest 5%.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow Initiative
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2018, the Adapt and Grow Initiative helped more than 76,000 jobseekers find employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, we are told that from 2016 to 2018, the Adapt and Grow Initiative has enabled more than 76,000 jobseekers to find employment.

sections.label: Survey underemployment rate
sections.summary: The survey found an underemployment rate of 4.3%, higher than MOM's 3.3% based solely on time criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The survey yielded an underemployment rate of 4.3%, which was higher than the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) rate of 3.3% based solely on time criteria.

sections.label: MOM underemployment figures
sections.summary: As at June 2018, MOM's underemployment rate was 3.3%, nearly 73,000 workers, and higher for the less educated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Turning now to MOM's figures, as at June 2018, the underemployed rate was 3.3%.
