sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even by MOM’s measure, the 3.3% translates into nearly 73,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The MOM statistics also suggest that underemployment affects those with less education more: while underemployment for university graduates is at 2.3%, for those with secondary education, this rises to nearly 4%, and for those with below secondary education, the underemployment rate is 5%.

sections.label: Gig economy job drawbacks
sections.summary: Gig workers lack paid help or family support and gig jobs come with hardly any employee benefits or CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They do not have paid help or family support and find it difficult to take time off regular work to attend to personal matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is well-known that gig economy jobs come with hardly any employee benefits, such as paid leave or bonuses, and do not attract CPF contributions, though I am aware that the Government is looking into improving terms and conditions for gig workers.

sections.label: Warrants of arrest for fines
sections.summary: Residents who do not attend Court face Warrants of Arrest over regulatory matters like parking and smoking fines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Time and again, I have seen residents who do not attend Court being subject to Warrants of Arrest over regulatory matters, such as parking and smoking fines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe more compassion can be shown in this area, such as to allow instalment payments for composition fines.

sections.label: Technology in arts and culture
sections.summary: Technology and innovation are key for arts and culture, with Digimuse and Digital Concerts cited as examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similar for the arts and culture, to allow it to continue to be relevant to audience needs and preferences and becoming an integral part of Singaporeans' lives and to enrich the soul of the nation, harnessing technology and innovation is the key and way forward for the arts and culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is interesting to note that The National Museum of Singapore has been utilising digital technology to innovate and enhance visitor experience to the museum under their Digimuse initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In January 2018, there was an open call for partners to submit digital art and innovation concepts that can benefit and elevate visitor experience at the museum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It eventually turned into an exhibition titled Digimuse Presents, which featured a diverse range of seven digitally led prototype projects to enhance the journey of cultural discovery for museum goers, allowing visitors to explore fresh perspectives of culture and heritage via a series of immersive virtual and augmented reality exhibits, dynamic conversations enabled by artificial intelligence (AI) and more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To date, Digimuse-related exhibitions and programmes have welcomed 92,000 visitors to the museum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over at the Singapore Chinese Orchestra, we started our Digital Concerts in 2017, streaming our concerts live to audiences in the comfort of their homes as well as for the international community.

sections.label: UK smart captioning glasses
sections.summary: The UK National Theatre uses smart captioning glasses showing dialogue transcripts and sound descriptions on lenses for people with hearing loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over in the UK, the National Theatre employ the use of smart captioning glasses, which allows people with hearing loss to enjoy performances; users will see a transcript of the dialogue and descriptions of the sound from a performance displayed on the lenses of glasses.

sections.label: Singapore arts technology initiatives
sections.summary: The National Museum's Digimuse drew close to 90,000 visitors, and other Singapore arts groups used technology in performances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National Museum has introduced the Digimuse initiative to enhance visitor experience by combining technology with arts and has attracted close to 90,000 visitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Chinese Orchestra and Zaobao.sg launched the first digital Chinese orchestra concert in the world in 2017 so that audiences around the world can all enjoy the music from the Singapore Chinese Orchestra.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 2019 International Arts Festival incorporated new technology elements into the stage setting which has not only increased the interactions between performers and audiences but also created a new narrative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Local arts group Finger Players will be presenting in March this year an inclusive performance to audiences with disabilities through the usage of close captioning and audio description.

sections.label: Call for digital arts collaboration
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Government, arts groups, IHLs, tech companies and researchers work together or start a research foundation for digital arts innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, I hope the Government, arts groups, IHLs, tech companies and researchers can work together or even start a research foundation to promote digital innovation in the arts and culture scene.

sections.label: School student government subsidy

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Consider, for example, the number of community gardens that have flourished in our heartlands.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I have 13 of such gardens in my own constituency and we are now planning our 14th garden.

sections.label: Bicentennial Community Fund and Bonus

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance announced two initiatives – the Bicentennial Community Fund and the Bicentennial Bonus – to support the commemoration.

sections.label: Colonialism's varying impact and commemoration aims
sections.summary: The speaker says colonialism's varying impact must be acknowledged and the commemoration should strengthen national ties and correct historical myths.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It has led some to wonder what would have happened if this region had not experienced colonialism.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, the first point I would like to make is that we need to acknowledge the varying impact of colonialism on the indigenous population and other populations.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And I share Minister Heng Swee Keat's call to build a caring and inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, this commemoration should aim to strengthen our ties as a nation by helping us better appreciate and understand the various communities' historical experiences and memories, as well as banish forever myths and misperceptions of our history that do damage to our communities.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In fact, historians have uncovered concrete evidence to suggest that Singapore was once a vibrant economic hub and not a fishing village waiting to be discovered by enlightened British imperialists.

sections.label: Toxic myth of the lazy native
sections.summary: The speaker says the colonial experience produced disturbing myths about the region, including the toxic myth of the lazy native.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Out of the colonial experience emerged many disturbing myths about this region, including the most toxic myth of the lazy native.

sections.label: Recognising less savoury colonial aspects
sections.summary: The speaker says commemorating the Bicentennial requires recognising less savoury colonial practices and supports celebrating 700 years of history.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we are to commemorate the Bicentennial, we must also recognise the less savoury aspects of it – practices and ideas designed to meet the needs and maximise the profits of the empire at the expense of the indigenous population.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In view of our long history, some historians have asked why not celebrate 700 years of our history?

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I support this idea as it would help us to better understand 1819 as one milestone among many.

sections.label: Precolonial history in school curriculum
sections.summary: Suggests considering the history curriculum in schools so students learn precolonial history and the region.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Arising from this, we could consider looking at our history curriculum in schools to ensure that students are well-versed in precolonial history as well as a deeper understanding of the region.

sections.label: Museums and precolonial history spaces
sections.summary: Says museums can do more to have spaces on precolonial history and give access to archeological finds.

sentences.speaker: Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our museums can do more to have spaces that touch on the subject of precolonial history and to give people access to the archeological finds.

sections.label: REACH feedback on Budget

sentences.text: In a quick sensing exercise by the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) after the Budget announcement, several people gave feedback that this year's Budget is a compassionate one which makes provisions for those in need.

sections.label: CHAS announcements and review
sections.summary: Lauds the CHAS announcements, having previously asked in the House for a review of CHAS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: On this point, I laud the announcements on CHAS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I had on previous occasions in this House asked for a review of CHAS.

sections.label: Containers diverted and award winner

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would also like to mention Siti Noor Mastura, the winner of The Straits Times Singaporean of the Year 2018.

sections.label: CPF top-up for older Singaporeans
sections.summary: Supports the CPF top-up of up to S$1,000 for Singaporeans aged 50 to 64 with less than S$60,000 retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: They worked hard to support the dreams of their children and sharing the Bicentennial Bonus with them is a meaningful way to recognise their contributions.

sections.label: Closing wage gap for women
sections.summary: The passage states there is some way to go to close the wage gap between men and women, support women returning to the workforce or leaving caregiving, and empower women to take up leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, there is some way to go to close the wage gap between men and women, to support women who return to the workforce after having children or when they transit from their caregiving roles by reducing structural barriers and to empower women to take up leadership positions.

sections.label: M3 plan for Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: Last year, Minister in-charge of Muslim Affairs Mr Masagos Zulkifli charted a plan for the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore through M3.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, the Minister in-charge of Muslim Affairs Mr Masagos Zulkifli charted a plan for the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore through M3.

sections.label: Bicentennial Bonus CPF top-up for women

sections.label: Defence, security and diplomacy spending
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore is vulnerable to regional and world fluctuations, commends Digital Defence as the sixth pillar of Total Defence and the Home Team Science and Technology Agency, and commends investing about 30% of total expenditure in defence, security and diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also commend the move to invest about 30% of our total expenditure to support defence, security and diplomacy efforts as it is paramount to safeguard the sovereignty of Singapore and the well-being of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singapore Global Innovation Index ranking
sections.summary: Singapore is ranked 5th in the Global Innovation Index 2018, but the passage states more can and needs to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is ranked 5th in the world by the Global Innovation Index 2018 but we can do more, and we need to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The move to combine the current local and overseas internship programmes into a single Global Ready Talent Programme for students who are currently in IHLs is a step in the right direction.

sections.label: WIS changes for workers
sections.summary: The passage gives a case of a 35-year-old Singaporean earning $2,300 and proposes raising the WIS income cap, lowering the qualifying age to 30, and increasing the cash to CPF ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)

sentences.text: After CPF contribution, he takes home $1,840 and, even with the additional WIS top-up, it will only add up to $1,896.70 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, increasing the WIS qualifying income cap to $2,640 to help our workers, which is 60% of our median wage; second, to lower the qualifying age to 30 to include younger Singaporeans who are trying to settle down but are struggling to get by; third, to increase the cash to CPF ratio to 50:50 or even 60:40.

sections.label: Extending healthcare package to citizens
sections.summary: The passage requests the Minister to consider extending the package to all Singapore Citizens aged 60 to 69 this year, regardless of citizenship obtained by 1996.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I request the hon Minister to consider extending the package to all Singapore Citizens between the ages of 60 to 69 this year, irrespective of them having obtained citizenship by 1996.

sections.label: MediSave contribution rate basis
sections.summary: The passage states Goh Chok Tong announced a 6% MediSave contribution rate would suffice, and the 1983 Blue Paper based the rate on detailed computations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When introducing MediSave, Emeritus Senior Minister Goh Chok Tong, who was then Second Minister for Health, announced that a 6% contribution rate to MediSave would suffice for, and I quote, "most households to have sufficient savings in their MediSave accounts to cover their expected hospitalisation expenses." The Blue Paper on the National Health Plan published in 1983 based the MediSave contribution rate on detailed computations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Blue Paper projected that MediSave contributions from a typical three-generation family should cover the entire family’s expected hospitalisation costs, even assuming that the Government would only subsidise 50% of Class C actual costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Life expectancy at birth when MediSave was introduced was 72 years; today, it is 83.

sections.label: Strengthening institutions outside Executive
sections.summary: A sustainable Singapore depends on strengthening institutions outside the Government and Executive that can question assumptions, review policies and collaborate.

sentences.text: Because of the power that a strong Executive has to formulate and implement policies, a sustainable Singapore depends on strengthening institutions outside the Government and outside the Executive that can question assumptions, review policies and collaborate to find the best way forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are also non-partisan committees, such as the Joint Committee on Taxation, who play a statutory role in producing independent assessments of the effects of taxation.

sentences.text: The Minister for Education noted that Singaporeans are, overall, reasonably well-represented in local universities, at about 50-50.

sections.label: Citizenship priority for taxpayers

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Pakistan denied there was any training camp operating there and has since retaliated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There have been firefights in Kashmir and Indian aeroplanes have also been attacked, with one Indian Air Force (IAF) pilot allegedly captured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And this is particularly worrying because both are nuclear powers and the consequence of any miscalculation would be dire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And I think this has been, thanks to the hard work of our leadership team at multiple levels, including the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Transport and Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, the fact remains that there are two Malaysian vessels in our territorial waters and, if there is any escalation or threat to our sovereignty or territorial integrity, we have to ask ourselves the uncomfortable question of what we will do.

sections.label: Parliament debates and party views
sections.summary: Parliamentary debates reflect differing views and formalise policies into law, so giving voice to different views within a single party is essential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Politics and debates in this House, therefore, reflect what those differing views are, and, at the close of the debates, policies impacting society are formalised into law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, giving voice to different views within a single political party is essential for Singapore.

sections.label: Value of diverse party views
sections.summary: There is value in housing different views within a single political party, besides drawing from a broad slate of possibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Besides being able to draw from a broad slate of possibilities, there is value in housing different views within a single political party.

sections.label: Deliberation, differing views, persuasion
sections.summary: The passage states that policies from deliberation need not be compromise but possibility through persuasion, coupling differing views with party cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Coupling the ability to house members of differing views with the need for cooperation among members of a single party, the policies and directions that come out from the deliberative process is not necessarily one characterised by compromise, but one of possibility through persuasion.

sections.label: US tax code loopholes
sections.summary: The passage states the US tax code often contains loopholes from political bargains between Democrats wanting higher rates for the rich and Republicans preferring tax cuts for the rich.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, in order to get bipartisan support to pass legislation, the US tax code often contains loopholes due to political bargains that needed to be struck between the Democrats that desire higher rates for richer Americans and Republicans who prefer to reduce taxes for the rich.

sections.label: AfD enters German parliament
sections.summary: The passage states that in September 2017 the AfD became the first far-right party in Germany's national parliament since the 1950s, winning 94 seats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In Germany, in September 2017, the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) became the first far-right party to enter Germany's national parliament since the 1950s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It won 94 seats to become the third strongest party in the Bundestag, Germany's lower house of Parliament.

sections.label: Costs of 2013 US shutdown
sections.summary: The passage states the 2013 16-day shutdown delayed almost $4 billion in tax refunds and stalled home loans for 8,000 rural families, costing $2 billion to $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: During the 16-day shutdown in 2013, almost $4 billion in tax refunds were delayed, home loans for 8,000 rural families were stalled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to the Office of Management and Budget, the US lost an estimated $2 billion to $6 billion of economic growth during the 16-day shutdown in 2013.

sections.label: Debating tough decisions in Parliament
sections.summary: The passage states it is better to debate and decide tough decisions in Parliament rather than passing the buck, and supports the social compact in Budget 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, when we are faced with tough decisions, it is, in my view, much better to debate the ideas respectfully and holistically in Parliament, and decide in Parliament what the path to take for Singapore is, rather than passing the buck back to the good people who entrusted us with the decision-making duties in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I come back to this central issue of a social compact, which was a major plank in Minister Heng Swee Keat’s speech on Budget 2019 which I support.

sections.label: Drug stance and reviewing data
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker's hard stance against drugs and criminalising trafficking and consumption, but would review conclusions if objective data showed consumption is not harmful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As an example, Sir, some fellow Members of this House would know my hard stance against drugs and the need to criminalise the trafficking as well as the consumption of drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is because I humbly remain convinced that drugs are harmful, especially to the consumers and the communities around them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, if objective and "un-agended" data shows that the consuming of illicit drugs is not harmful, then I will review the data and test my conclusions again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For the record, as regards drugs, I am still of the view that we need to criminalise consumption.

sections.label: Merdeka Generation Package cost
sections.summary: The Merdeka Generation Package is estimated to cost over $8 billion and help close to half a million senior Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One highlight of this year's Budget is the Merdeka Generation Package (MGP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This package is estimated to cost over $8 billion in present value, and help close to half a million senior Singaporeans.

sections.label: Healthcare focus of package
sections.summary: The Government chose to focus the package's benefits on healthcare, which it calls the right priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: There are many ways the package could have been designed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But the Government chose to focus the benefits on healthcare, which is the right priority.

sections.label: Gratitude to Merdeka Generation
sections.summary: The $8 billion package conveys gratitude and respect for the Merdeka Generation and is not welfare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The MG contributed their youth and efforts and built the Singapore that we are proud of today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This $8 billion package conveys our gratitude and respect for the MG and cannot be considered as welfare.

sections.label: Social challenges and responses
sections.summary: The passage lists social challenges and calls for more public education, resource redistribution and community participation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Our experience has been admired and emulated by many around the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: However, our society construct is also exposed to some unique challenges: the advent of social media has the potential to aggravate fractures within our society through fake news and fear mongering – sensational pieces are always more attention-grabbing than run-of-the-mill news pieces; our changing demographics – an ageing society will assert more pressure on the working class; evolving expectations of citizens increase pressure on our Government to deliver better and faster; religious radicalism plants dangerous seeds of antagonism and mistrust which could destroy our social bonds; and, of course, there is a risk of widening wealth and digital gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, if fake news or radicalism gains momentum, our social fabric, so carefully built and maintained over the past decades, could be torn if people doubt and confront one another over what is true and what they think is true.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, we need to invest more in public education to inoculate our people against the poison of fake news and radicalism; we need to redistribute resources more to reduce the gaps; we need to create opportunities and empower our people to participate in the community more.

sections.label: Budget for youths and poor
sections.summary: The Budget should set aside financial resources to support youths and help the poor and vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Others believe in building a fairer, more equitable society and they contribute their energy and time to help the poor and vulnerable in society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is important that our Budget set aside enough financial resources annually to go into supporting the priorities and efforts of our youths, as well as in mentoring them and developing their talents so that, in time, they will be able to lead Singapore to a new level.

sections.label: Government resources for MGP
sections.summary: On social issues, only the Government has the resources to mount a major move like the MGP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On social issues, only the Government has the resources to mount a major move like the MGP.

sections.label: Building a strong united Singapore
sections.summary: Some challenge current thinking and others refine policies, to help Singaporeans thrive and build a strong, united Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Some challenge our current thinking, while others help us refine our policies over time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It is to help Singaporeans thrive and build a strong, united Singapore.

sections.label: Responding to speeches and policy specifics
sections.summary: After listening to over 12 hours of speeches, the speaker cannot address every point; colleagues will engage on specifics within their Ministries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Listening to over 12 hours of your speeches in the last two days and this morning, I realise that it is not possible for me to address each of the points you have raised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: My colleagues will engage you in the specifics of policies within their Ministry's purview.

sections.label: Three approaches to planning
sections.summary: Plans put people at the centre, plan long term while adapting to changing circumstances, and work in partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, we put people at the centre of our plans, strategies and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Second, we plan long term while taking an adaptive approach to respond to changing circumstances and needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Third, we do all of this together, working in partnership.

sections.label: Primary school fees
sections.summary: Parents pay $13 each month per child for primary school fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Parents pay $13 each month per child for primary school fees.

sections.label: School CCAs and Edusave awards
sections.summary: CCAs are part of schools and Government-funded, unlike systems where parents pay outside classes; EAGLES and Edusave Skills Award recognise non-academic excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: When I was an Education Minister, I visited many school systems around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And what struck me in many of the school systems was that, when I asked, "If your child or your student wants to learn Arts, Music, Dance, Sports, what do they do?" And in many of the school systems, the answer was, "Well, they have to join outside classes." And I asked, "How do you pay for it?" They said, "Well, we as parents pay for it." Whereas in our school system, CCAs to develop our students' interest and to develop them in diverse ways are part of the schools' system and funded by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Edusave Award for Achievement, Good Leadership and Service (EAGLES) and the Edusave Skills Award are just some of the ways we recognise students who demonstrate excellence for achievements, beyond academic.

sections.label: Programmes for regional exposure
sections.summary: Plans in this and the last two Budgets help tertiary students, young workers and aspiring leaders build friendships and understand the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In this and the last two Budgets, I set out plans that will help our tertiary students, young workers and aspiring leaders to build friendships with peoples and understand our region better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: These include the Global Innovation Alliance, the Leadership Development Initiative, and the Global Ready Talent Programme.

sections.label: Workfare not welfare schemes
sections.summary: The passage states Workfare is given instead of welfare, citing the Workfare Training Support scheme and enhanced Workfare Income Supplement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This is why we give Workfare, not welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have the Workfare Training Support scheme to encourage skills upgrading, and the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS), which I announced enhancements to this year.

sections.label: CPF retirement savings support
sections.summary: The passage states CPF helps workers save for retirement with a risk-free return and extra interest on certain balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: On the whole, our broad-based schemes are designed to provide them with more support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We help our workers save for retirement through the Central Provident Fund (CPF), which provides a risk-free return, with an extra 1% interest on the first $60,000 of CPF balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Those who are aged 55 and above receive an additional 1% for the first $30,000 of balances.

sections.label: Schemes for lower-income groups
sections.summary: The passage states KidSTART, Fresh Start Housing Scheme and Silver Support help lower-income and old-age groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about the need to uplift these groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have put in place schemes, such as KidSTART and the Fresh Start Housing Scheme, which help the lower-income get back on their feet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For those in their old age, Silver Support provides a supplement for those who had low incomes through life and little family support.

sections.label: Bicentennial Bonus CPF top-up
sections.summary: The passage states the CPF top-up in this year's Bicentennial Bonus supports women who did not work and had low CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In particular, the CPF top-up in this year’s Bicentennial Bonus will support women who did not work and, therefore, had low CPF savings for retirement.

sections.label: Ageing committee and sea levels
sections.summary: The passage states the first committee on ageing was set up in 1982 and infrastructural plans address rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, the first committee on ageing was set up in 1982 when the proportion of Singaporeans aged 65 and above was only 5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We are looking at various infrastructural plans to protect us from rising sea levels due to climate change, the effects of which are projected to hit us sometime between 2050 and 2100.

sections.label: Manufacturing base and Global-Asia node
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore keeps a strong manufacturing base and must strengthen its position as a Global-Asia node.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We also continue to have a strong manufacturing base, despite increasing competition from other economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We must push ahead to strengthen Singapore’s position as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: Productivity, innovation, Dependency Ratio Ceiling
sections.summary: It calls for improving productivity and innovation at industry and firm level, and states the Dependency Ratio Ceiling for services was cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: What we need now is to double down on improving productivity and innovation at the industry and firm level, in particular, through a targeted, tailored approach to get firms of different types to adapt and transform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have made the difficult but necessary move of cutting the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) levels for the services sector.

sections.label: Rationalising grants and financing schemes
sections.summary: It states grants under PSG, EDG and PACT were rationalised, and eight financing schemes will be streamlined into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To reduce the number of schemes for firms to navigate, we rationalised grants that served similar objectives under the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG), Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) and Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT) programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This year, we will streamline eight financing schemes into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS).

sections.label: CHAS subsidies for chronic illnesses
sections.summary: It states CHAS subsidies will be expanded later this year to provide universal coverage for chronic illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Later this year, we will expand the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) subsidies to provide universal coverage for chronic illnesses.

sections.label: Singaporean youths post-secondary education
sections.summary: It states that more than nine in 10 Singaporean youths can expect to go on to a post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Today, more than nine in 10 Singaporean youths can expect to go on to a post-secondary education – nine in 10.

sections.label: Cohort-based approach to healthcare costs
sections.summary: It states a calibrated cohort-based approach is fair to generations, and warns rash promises like universal benefits could burden future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Building on our substantial base of permanent healthcare schemes, a calibrated cohort-based approach is fair to different generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: If we continue to take a responsible and long-term approach to planning, younger Singaporeans need not fear that they will end up with a disproportionate share of the cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But if we lose this discipline and make rash promises, like universal benefits regardless of circumstances, I would worry for our future generations.

sections.label: PSA workers reskilled at Pasir Panjang
sections.summary: It states PSA reskilled and upskilled over 1,300 workers who moved from city terminals to use new technology at Pasir Panjang Terminals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: PSA has reskilled and upskilled over 1,300 workers who transitioned from city terminals, to use the new technology at the Pasir Panjang Terminals over the past few years.

sections.label: LEAD programme enhancements
sections.summary: Budget enhancements to the LEAD programme will further strengthen the role TACs play.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The enhancements to the Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD) programme which I announced in this Budget will further strengthen the role that TACs play.

sections.label: Scale-up SG and Innovation Agents
sections.summary: The Scale-up SG and pilot Innovation Agents programmes announced in this Budget help businesses identify challenges and scale quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This is to help them identify and overcome the unique challenges they face, and scale their businesses quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I announced the Scale-up SG programme and the pilot Innovation Agents programme this Budget, which will help in this area.

sections.label: VCF funding and donation tax deduction
sections.summary: In 2017 $100 million was set aside for the fourth VCF tranche, and qualifying donations get a 250% tax deduction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In 2017, we set aside $100 million for the fourth tranche of VCF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The 250% tax deduction that we offer today on qualifying donations is also one of the most generous tax deduction schemes worldwide.

sections.label: GST increase for spending needs
sections.summary: The GST increase is needed to support structural increases in healthcare spending and other needs like preschool education and security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The GST increase is needed to support structural increases in healthcare spending, among other important needs, like preschool education and security.

sections.label: MOH patient bill subsidies
sections.summary: MOH expects to spend $6.1 billion in 2019 to subsidise patient bills through existing permanent schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: MOH expects to spend $6.1 billion in 2019 alone to subsidise patient bills through existing permanent schemes that all Singaporeans enjoy.

sections.label: OECD revenue needs versus GST
sections.summary: The median OECD government is estimated to need additional revenues of 6.5 percentage points of GDP by 2060, while the GST increase raises about 0.7 percentage points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The median OECD government is estimated to require additional revenues of 6.5 percentage points of GDP by 2060; 6.5 percentage point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To put it in perspective, we expect to raise about 0.7 percentage points of GDP with the planned 2 percentage point GST increase.

sections.label: Revenue and expenditure estimates accuracy
sections.summary: Actual revenue and expenditure figures have generally been within +/- 4% of original estimates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Actual revenue and expenditure figures have generally been within +/- 4% of our original estimates.

sections.label: Japan and Hong Kong estimate errors
sections.summary: Japan's revenue estimates had about 11% margin of error over five years, while Hong Kong averaged 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Japan’s revenue estimates, for example, had a margin of error of about 11% over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Hong Kong, a small open economy like ours, averaged slightly better, at 8%.

sections.label: 2008 Global Financial Crisis funding
sections.summary: Accumulated savings funded $15.6 billion, three-quarters of the $20.5 billion Resilience Package, with the rest from past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: During the Global Financial Crisis in 2008, our accumulated savings allowed us to fund $15.6 billion, or three-quarters of the $20.5 billion Resilience Package, with the remainder being funded from past Reserves.

sections.label: Studying borrowing for infrastructure
sections.summary: The Government is studying borrowing as a tool to finance major, long-term infrastructure and will announce plans in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As I mentioned in the Budget Statement, the Government is studying the option of borrowing carefully as a tool to finance major, long-term infrastructure, and will announce our plans in due course.

sections.label: Borrowing for long-term projects
sections.summary: Borrowing can fairly and efficiently finance projects with lumpy upfront costs and multi-generational benefits instead of raising taxes sharply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As these projects have lumpy upfront costs and benefits that span many generations, borrowing can be a fair and efficient tool to finance and spread out these costs, instead of raising taxes sharply to fund them.

sections.label: Borrowing and recurrent spending
sections.summary: Borrowing does not create new revenues for recurrent spending; it converts concentrated spending into smoother loan repayments with interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Borrowing does not create new revenues for recurrent spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It merely converts a concentrated lump of spending in a few years into a smoother stream of loan repayment with interest.

sections.label: Review of eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The Government will continue to regularly review eligibility criteria so schemes benefit intended groups while remaining practical to implement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Government will continue to regularly review the eligibility criteria to ensure our schemes benefit the intended groups, whilst being practical to implement.

sections.label: New Buyer's Stamp Duty tier
sections.summary: In last year's Budget, a new tier was introduced for Buyer's Stamp Duty on properties valued above a million dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In last year's Budget, I introduced a new tier for the Buyer's Stamp Duty for value of properties in excess of a million dollars.

sections.label: Early Turnover Scheme for vehicles
sections.summary: The 2013 Early Turnover Scheme helped over 40,000 commercial goods vehicles switch to cleaner, more fuel-efficient diesel vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In 2013, we introduced the Early Turnover Scheme (ETS) which has helped more than 40,000 commercial goods vehicles switch to cleaner and more fuel-efficient diesel vehicles.

sections.label: Fall in diesel taxis
sections.summary: Diesel taxis decreased by more than 30% from 23,700 in 2016 to 15,100 in 2018 as companies switch to electric and electric-hybrid taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The number of diesel taxis has also decreased by more than 30% from 23,700 in 2016 to 15,100 in 2018, as taxi companies switch to electric and electric-hybrid taxis.

sections.label: Subsidies, top-ups and rebates
sections.summary: Subsidies keep school and university fees low, PGP and MGP ease healthcare costs, and this year bring top-ups and income tax rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Without these subsidies, families would have to pay more than 60 times the current fees for their children in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: University fees would also be four times what Singaporean students currently pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The PGP and MGP ease healthcare costs for their parents and, in so doing, help with their families’ overall expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This year, many will receive a number of top-ups, such as to their children’s Edusave or Post-Secondary Education Accounts (PSEA) and their parents' CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: All who pay personal income tax will receive a rebate.

sections.label: Duration of measure
sections.summary: The speaker says it is going to last for quite a number of years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: All I can say is that it is going to last for quite a number of years.

sections.label: NIRC revenue over four years
sections.summary: Budget annexes show NIRC, including NII and NIR, reached $62 billion over the last four years and may reach about $80 billion over a full five-year term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, you have to earn your keep before spending, so to speak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But if you look at one of the Budget annexes on the Analysis of Revenue and Expenditure, based on the NIRC component which includes both the Net Investment Income (NII) and NIR, for the last four years, it has come up to $62 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And based on the trending, it would probably to be about $80 billion over the course of one Government's term, provided it runs for its full five years.

sections.label: Respondents disagree on higher taxes
sections.summary: Slightly more than 40% of respondents disagree with paying higher taxes to fund increased social spending on the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The response is, slightly more than 40% of respondents disagree to paying higher taxes to fund increased social spending on the elderly.

sections.label: $6.1 billion healthcare subsidies
sections.summary: The $6.1 billion spent on this is a subsidy on a subsidised rate, with MGP and PGP built on existing structural healthcare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The $6.1 billion that it is spending on this alone will give you an idea of that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As I said earlier, we already have many structural subsidies which are already built into our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: So, the MGP and PGP are built on top of what we already have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This is a subsidy on a subsidised rate.

sections.label: MGP, PGP and NIRC funding
sections.summary: IPS survey respondents vary on funding current or future needs, and the MGP and PGP set aside for long-term care must not be confused with NIRC use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As Members can see in the IPS survey, respondents vary in their comments whether they should be funding current, whether they should be funding future and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We must not confuse the MGP and PGP that have been set aside to fund these long-term care programmes with the use of NIRC.
